I don't really review early access games but this time I am making an exception. The reason for that is that Estranged Act I is a great Half-Life 2 mod. I enjoyed every minute of it and when I saw the page for the second act was up and running I immediately jumped in to try it.
There are a couple of things you can notice immediately. First, the game looks superb. Way better than its predecessor - this is understandable as Unreal Engine 4 is responsible for making the 2nd act work. You'll also notice that the game is incomplete. There are some puzzle sequences and a couple of enemies and in 30 minutes you are done. It was a bit disappointing as the menu allows us to launch several chapters but these are separated by a maximum of 5 minutes gameplay only.
With the incomplete status come several bugs / glitches. There are texture pop-ups here and there; occasionally you fall through the level and some sound effects are missing. I do believe, however, all will be completed in due course. It is my understanding that this is a hobby project for the creators so they cannot really rush it. I have to admit I expected more glitches and way more content (as in cutscenes et al) but I am happy it turned out this way.
At this point I can only recommend Act II for those who've already played (and liked) the first episode. While the graphics are completely different I could feel they are trying to redo the exact same atmosphere this time, as well. Good luck for that! I'll make sure I'll check this periodically for any major updates.

This is an interesting game about exploring "The Deep Web" trying to find pieces of a URL so you can go to "The Red Room" now I will list my pros and cons

Cons

Verdict
-Terrifying and Tense Atmosphere

An intriguing point & click adventure game by developers of Lords of The Fallen, Venetica and Ankh series. It was first released in 2010 in Germany, but it has never been localised into English until now. Steam version comes with both English texts and dialogues.
Anna and Lex survive a ship catastrophe and end up on a deserted brigantine full of strange equipment and machines. They have to uncover the mystery behind its history and find a way to reach dry land. Gameplaywise it's a traditional point and click game without any arcade elements - forget about QTE's, shooting, timed riddles and other stuff that is currently being introduced into games of this genre. There is, however, one very interesting system implemented - your decisions alter the relationship between Anna and Lex. It may not change the course of the story, but it changes the way they speak to each other, which is a nice addition abd makes the characters more believeable.
Black Sails is advertised as a scary game, but it's not really true - there are some minor jump-scares, but it's nothing as intense as Amnesia, Soma or other horror adventures. It's more of a mystery game with some surprising twists and moments that make you change the theory you had about what's going on. There are also multiple ways your adventure can end. The twist behind the story is interesting and well executed. At one point towards the end I really had goosebumps because of what I learned about the ship and my characters. I'd say that the ending alone is worth the price.
Unfortunately, not everything is as good as the ending. Black Sails can get irritating at times.  The font used in letters and notes you find on your way is extremely hard to read and the camera behaves strange from time to time forcing you to take a few steps backwards in order to go forward. It also crashed for me twice. Maybe it's my PC's fault but make sure to save your progress as often as possible anyway.
It's a short and easy game - if you are experienced with adventure games, you'll complete it and watch all ending variants in about 4 hours. This doesn't change the fact that I had a lot of fun with it and finished the game with pleasure. I would recommend it to beginners or players that are more interested in the story than in solving riddles.
PROS:
+ dense atmosphere
+ surprising and well executed story
+ possibility to shape relation between characters
+ nice and easy
CONS:
- font used in notes and letters is hard to read
- sometimes the camera behaves strange
- short

Lost Planet proves that Capcom still knows how to make a fun and engaging game. As a single-player game, Lost Planet provides a thrilling action-adventure that really feels like a fun adventure. You go places, and despite the game taking place on a snow-bound E.D.N III, there's a lot of different vistas to visit in the game which host a wide variety of enemies, ranging from armed dudes to giant robots to even larger giant bugs. What's even cooler is that if you can get your hands on a mech, you can ride that mech! A lot of them have unique features making them useful for various situations, on top of that they can be equiped with the various mech weapons you'll no doubt find throughout the levels.
When you're not in a mech, you have the same kind of mobility. You can equip two of the various no-frills weapons that are available in the game as well as a single type of grenade. What weapons you decide to take with you make a significant impact on your playstyle. Rockets are handy to keep on you should a giant bug come at you (Which happens often,) but ammunition is few and far between, forcing you to stick with a different weapon until the situation calls for explosives. If you happen to come across any large mech-weapons but there are no mechs to be seen, you can still pick them up and use em, but you can't switch weapons without dropping them. On top of that, you have a grappling hook that you can use to get to higher levels and for (slightly) speedier travel. The only problem that I had is that getting hit can lock you down for a moment longer than you might want to be, Monster Hunter fans will know what I'm talking about.
But perhaps the biggest gameplay feature is the thermal energy sysytem. While you do have a typical health bar, your health will regenerate as long as you have energy, which is dropped by enemies and can be found from destroying some of the game's destructable environments. The thing is, that energy drains over time, even moreso when you're doing various activities such as jumping, or being in a mech. This, in my opinion, gives the game a sense of urgency. You'll be making decisions for yourself, "Should I keep moving forward or take the time to look for spare energy?"
The boss fights in the game are big, monstrous and provide a good amount of challenge, a lot of the time I found myself in various do-or-die situations where I was down to my last rocket and was running dangerously low on energy. These are the kinds of bosses that I love to fight, ones with big, high damaging attacks, health bars the length of the screen, and a lot of variety to make them stand out from the other enemies you'll find yourself facing. And defeating them feels oh so satisfying.
All in all, Lost Planet feels like a proper game. This game is a textbook example of how a good action-adventure game should play and a reminder that while Capcom tends to make some really dumb decisions, they still know how to create a memorable experience that stands out amongst the crowd.

Our adventure begins when our character, Anna and Lex, who's evidently isn't the niceste person in the world, are involved in a shipwreck while traveling to Europe. While trying to survive, they spot a boat engulfed in a ghostly mist. They board it. and so the game begins. You must progress through the ship and find a way to get to land.
As the usual point and click adventure game, you will have solve diverse environmental puzzles. They are all pretty logic so you should be able to progress just fine without looking things up, although this is affected sometimes by some things that are placed in places a bit too dark or obstructed to check, and sometimes using the mouse over the object you want doesn't always work, so you can be fooled to think something wasn't possible but it was just fault of the game not registering it properly. Anyhow, the puzzles are good and engaging, so you won't be bored by them or spend hours trying to decipher horribly over-cryptic things like in some other P&Cs.
In your conversations with Lex you will have different dialogue options that will affect your relationship with him. Positive, neutral or negative. It will change some of his dialogue he has, and a minor gameplay effect (he might help you if you act positive or just be a rude idiot if you act negative). Either way, he's a pretty unlikeable character that barely does anything to help at all while you solve everything, but that's actually somewhat justified for story reasons, so it's understandable and it works well.
Throughout the ship you will also find several notes detailing the past of the misterious ship. as well as some visions of people of that time. You must figure out what truly happened to this cursed ship and its inhabitants.
The game is somewhat graphically outdated, even for a game released in 2011. However, it has a strong artstyle that makes up for it. You will find some poor textures here and there, but overall it looks pleasant to the eye and actively contributes to create a creepy atmosphere.
Speaking of that creepy atmosphere, both the visuals and sound do well at create a unnerving feeling throughout the game, with you not being sure what's coming next. (although the game could use some expanded soundtrack. The game is perhaps too quiet at times). The whole ship makes you wonder what may've happened here.
Regarding voice acting in English, Anna's alright but I found that Lex was too monotone and not much expression. While I guess it's a decent result overall, I'd say for you to play it in the original German voices as they have better voice acting, and as well as voiced elements that are not in the english version.(Anna in German narrates the intro cutscene, and reads the notes you find outloud. This does not happen in English)
The game is a bit on the short side 3/4 hours, and it does feel that ends a little bit too soon, but for the price of 7.5$ that's pretty understandable and well worth it.
I'd recommend this to any classic 3D P&C fan, it does it's job pretty well, and it's worth the asking price.
My only grievance with the game was a bug that appeared a few times where the game would lose voice sound and eventually crash. Happened 3 times in my playthrough. I expect that it will be patched fast so not much of an issue. I also had a save bug where the the save dissapeared and I had to start the game, but it only happened that one time.
7/10

** PARTIAL SPOILERS (NOT STORYLINE-RELATED) **
PLAY THIS GAME! This game was a surprise hit with me. For years, people have been lauding this game as spectacular but for some reason, I always just viewed it as overrated from any previews that I looked at. I really can't say why.
But I hadn't looked at the game in a while and decided, what the heck, I'll get it. Biggest surprise ever.
I found this game scarier and more engrossing than many other horror games that I've played, and I'm a huge horror game fan.
For the review:
+ The graphics are really good if you have a system to run everything highly.
+ The sound fits perfectly. The dialog, for the most part, is well-done. The screams of people through the walls, the sounds of the Gatherers, the Shadow... everything is well done. And the music, when there, is pretty eerie.
+ The design of the castle as a whole is great. I like the layout and the hub areas that the game has you reach. Each time I set forth towards a new area from a given hub, I felt like I was starting a whole new adventure.
+ The atmosphere is just spot-on. If you allow yourself to be taken into the story and the world, you will find yourself breathless and scared. I know I did, many times, and there are many horror games that I can make it through without much fear. Any time a Gatherer was around, I felt like I was going to have a panic attack. Note that if you let yourself get killed 100 times and then just stop caring, you'll ruin the dynamic. I avoided them as much as possible and only died once, due to a game glitch.
- Mechanics-wise, sometimes I just had trouble grabbing certain objects, or I'd get stuck in doorways or holes in walls so on (even when properly crouching). Not that big of a buzzkill, though.
- The brute towards the end of the game in the Chancel glitched. He got stuck on the bridge leading towards the exit and he just spun around in circles. Exiting and coming back did nothing, for some reason. This glitch led to my only death in the game as I tried to just jump around him.
- There were visual errors here and there (read: they were NOT the hallucinations!) as things would pop up in my face like what looked like pieces of wood or pillars, then sometimes the walls glitched out a little.
- While the game was pretty lengthy and had a good environment, I still wish that there was more. Some of the places were very creepy in their own right, but they could've been extended, in my opinion. Just a simple example: the Morgue. I dreaded going in there, and while still scary, I was very disappointed to find out that it was only really two main rooms with a single monster. I know that the Morgue shouldn't have been gigantic, but perhaps there could have been a hidden area? Again, part of that is just wishing that every area was huge... though I probably wouldn't have completed the game if that were true.
- The "good ending" was a bit disappointing and short-lived.
=====
I'm sure there's other flaws I didn't really touch on, but that's because, for the most part, I don't remember many of them. That's simply because the game was good enough and it kept me captivated. As a whole, terrifying and well worth playing.

There is very little to say about the amazingness of this game. So instead I will put a recipe for pancakes.
\
Makes: 4 to 6 servings
Time: 20 minutes
It’s amazing how quickly you can whip up this batter.  Store it, covered, in the refrigerator for up to 2 days.  Adjust the consistency of the batter with either more milk or more flour as you like. Recipe from How to Cook Everything.
2 cups all-purpose flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
1/2 teaspoon salt
1 tablespoon sugar (optional)
2 eggs
11/2 to 2 cups milk
2 optional tablespoons melted and cooled butter, plus
unmelted butter for cooking, or use a neutral oil like
grapeseed or corn
1. Heat a griddle or large skillet over medium-low heat while you make the batter.
2. Mix together the dry ingredients. Beat the eggs into 11/2 cups of the milk, then stir in the 2 tablespoons cooled melted butter if you’re using it. Gently stir this mixture into the dry ingredients, mixing only enough to moisten the flour; don’t worry about a few lumps. If the batter seems thick, add a little more milk.
3. Use a little butter or oil each time you add batter, unless your skillet is truly nonstick. When the butter foam subsides or the oil shimmers, ladle batter onto the griddle or skillet, making any size pancakes you like.  Adjust the heat as necessary; usually, the first batch will require higher heat than subsequent batches. The idea is to brown the bottom in 2 to 4 minutes, without burning it. Flip when bubbles appear in the center of the pancakes and the bottoms are cooked; they won’t hold together well until they’re ready.
4. Cook until the second side is lightly browned, a couple more minutes, and serve or hold on an ovenproof plate in a 200°F oven for up to 15 minutes.

I'd rather not give this game a 10/10 just for being "retro-style" and reminding me of the "good ol' days". Instead, I'm judging based on how it is as a game alone, not what it stands for.
That being said, however, Shovel Knight is still an absolutley fantastic game.
Pros:
-Challenging gameplay. The combination of platforming challenges, tricky enemies, and the fact that you control a somewhat slow character force the player to find the best possible way to navigate each of the game's various challenges.
-Content. Shovel Knight packs plenty of secrets into each level, and it even includes a second story. There are also some weapon and armor upgrades, which slightly afffect the experience.
-Presentation. I know I said I was against using the game's retro style as a justification for its quality, but that doesn't mean it's not worth mentioning. The music is catchy and fitting for each stage, and the graphics are colorful and show off the wacky caracters and environments quite well.
-Humor. A minor thing, but this game is silly. Goofy characters and bad puns.
Cons:
-Challenging Gameplay. I know I praised the gameplay before, but I want you to remember that this game is hard, and it sometimes simply isn't fair. Sometimes you'll get punished for not having lightning-fast reflexes, other times you'll fall into a pit for trying to attack an enemy. Speakng of which, the instant-death in this game is incredibly prolific. Bottomless pits and spikes are abundant, and you are left with little to do about it other than die over and over until you get it right. Dying not only takes you back to one of the stage's infrequent checkpoints, but also causes you to lose gold, unless you can retrieve it.
Overall, great game. Buy it if you want a challenge.

Once upon a time, I tried Civilization V. I discovered it was buggy. What I did play was really fun though. So my in-laws bought me Civilization III, which was really fun. I then saw that Civilization IV was on sale, along with the expansions, so I bought the main game and a couple of the expansions. I am currently enjoying the happily ever after.
This is one of the most addictive games I have ever played. My husband and I are enjoying a hotseat match in which I am sure will end in a bloodbath. In Civilization IV: Beyond the Sword I am preparing to conquer the world with my mighty Celtic army. Civilization IV is an awesome strategy game in which almost anything is possible. There are so many different leaders to choose, and many different ways to beat the game. Sure, you could do a military victory, but you can also win diplomatically, artistically, and financially. There is also the Space Race...
For those of you kind of wary of strategy titles, let me assure you this is a very newbie friendly game. There are a variety of difficulties, and very detailed tutorials to help out. Also, being turn based has a huge advantage in being able to think out what you want to do. Having played Paradox Interactive titles like Victoria II, this is a far cry from the level of complexity found in those games. Nor is it very concerned with historical authenticity. When I first played as Boudicca, a warrior queen of the Celts, I expected to run into one of the Caesars, but instead I ran into General Bismark! My husband demonstrated some interesting divergents from history by having his Germans found Judaism 8), Christianity, and Islam. By what should have been mid-early Dark Ages, his musketmen were busy conquering the Russian Civilization. By the Industrial Revolution, his assorted tanks were conquering the world. He then won peacefully by using the UN to vote himself as the ruler of the world. Yeah...you definitely couldn't do that in a Paradox Interactive title.
I know I have many many more hours of enjoyment awaiting me in Civilization IV. This is a great game to play solo or with others. I can't wait to explore all the possibilities.

2/5 - Avoid unless you're really into the series
Cut through swathes of repetitive and somewhat uninspired monsters as a scantily clad lady weilding a lazer gun! If that's all you want from a game, then give sacred 2 a whirl. Some games do the b-movie thing well, see Typing of the Dead if you want a game that nails the vibe perfectly, and while Sacred 2's qualitative shortcomings are at times hilarious, these moments did not come often enough to really keep me entertained.
I might be missing the point here, but the lack of strong narrative, the ambiguous quests, terrible voice acting and implausible technological gaps between the player and your enemies made me wonder how effort really went into this game.
Everything about Sacred 2 either frustrated or failed to engage me and after a good few hours I simply gave up; I didn't want to just be clicking on an endless stream of monsters with no real interst in why for any longer.
While Sacred 2's character designs and progression systems have always been genuinely novel, the world that your character inhabits feels a little underdeveloped:
The open world vibe is totally subverted by linear quests and map design; when you get to a new place, you walk a set path around the area like you're on a go kart track rather than exploring and engaging with it. The side quests are uninspiring and revolve around the usual getting items, rescuing trapped elves and picking herbs.
The monsters are repetitive and while there are often quite a few of them to cut through, there's not enough diversity to differentiate engagements or to create any real challenges.
The environments feel devoid of personality; you walk through cities of people having randomly generated conversations which make little sense; it's like being trapped inside a bad parody of a game world, which can be funny at times but it becomes tiresome quickly.
The camera is oddly positioned and always left me craning my neck to see what's coming up ahead. Either when zoomed out or in I just couldn't see more than a few paces in front of me. Given that the camera follows the rotation of the player it can get a little disorientating at times, kind of like being trapped in a tumble dryer full of orcs.
Maybe I've been ruined by RPGs which either do the action better (D3 & Dark souls) or the story better (Dungeon Siege 3 & Skyrim) or both (the Witcher 2), but I really am starting to expect a little more substance from ARPGs. In a market as flooded as this one I really recommend looking elsewhere, it's a shame because this title has potential but it's let down by phoned in mechanics and a lack of attention to detail.

If I were to describe this game in three words, I would think of three words that describe this game, and eventually I would come up with these words: "It is hard." In the game, you hae to run around solving puzzles with a lantern that runs on oil that is not often found, you also have to stay in the light as to not lose some of your sanity. You also get tinderboxes, which you can use to light stationery candles and wall-mounted torches. There are potions you can use to regain sanity, and solving puzzles can also regain sanity. But. There is a twist to this game. Every once-in-a-while, you will come upon a weird background music, it will be a sort of fast-paced, loud, and sudden kind of music. If you hear this music, then you should immediately look for somewhere to hide. The best places to hide are in closets. There music is triggered by an enemy Gatherer. There are two main Gatherers: a Grunt and a Brute, there are also two other monsters. The Grunt is recognized by the half-ripped jaw that lays across its chest, it is sort of slow, but does damage if you get cornered, it also breaks down doors. The Brute is recognized by the blade it has for an arm, it is fast, do not run down a long hallway with this thing chasing you, it does twice as much damage as the Grunt and it breaks down doors twice as fast, it is, however, not as common as the Grunt. The third monster is commonly known as the water monster. It is completely invisible, except for when it moves, when it moves it makes splashes, it can not leave the water, so take any time on dry land as you can. The fourth monster is the Suitor. The Suitor is not in the main game, it is in the Justine campaign. It is recognized by the dragging chain noises and moaning that it makes. It is completely blind, but, it is very thorough in their search to find you, especially the final one. The main mission is to solve the puzzles and avoid the Gatherers at all costs, since you can't fight, it is best to hide. You do this until you make the final confrontation with Alexander.

I've been a huge fan since classic Flashpoint but I've found each new version only gets worse.  They keep piling the milsim details on top but the interface doesn't keep up.  There's steep learning curves with each game and it's very hard to set controls to something that doesn't feel like my character is drunk, and vehicle controls are beyond awful.  A better tutorial that really lays out all the controls might help, but perhaps I've just become too "casual" to enjoy these games anymore.  After an hour and checking the controls I couldn't even figure out how to change the firing mode on my gun.  In the very first tutorial mission it told me to go prone and fire at targets, but by going prone I could no longer aim side to side without my gun aiming up for some reason, possibly because of my body position or terrain.  Once again, they've tried to pack too much "realism" into the game without the controls/interface to support it.  I really liked the addition of being able to rest/attach guns onto cover and the game is gorgeous, but being a simple infantry soldier shouldn't require the use of nearly every key and ctrl and shift key combo to play.  I also could not read any of the grid text on maps as the text was far too small and not at all friendly to anyone who has red/green colour issues.
Possibly if I had put a few more hours into this and tweaked the interface and fought the learning curve I'd have enjoyed it, I ended up enjoying Arma and Arma 2, but I've found no game has ever recaptured the simple joy of Operation Flashpoint.

I'd rather not give this game a 10/10 just for being "retro-style" and reminding me of the "good ol' days". Instead, I'm judging based on how it is as a game alone, not what it stands for.
That being said, however, Shovel Knight is still an absolutley fantastic game.
Pros:
-Challenging gameplay. The combination of platforming challenges, tricky enemies, and the fact that you control a somewhat slow character force the player to find the best possible way to navigate each of the game's various challenges.
-Content. Shovel Knight packs plenty of secrets into each level, and it even includes a second story. There are also some weapon and armor upgrades, which slightly afffect the experience.
-Presentation. I know I said I was against using the game's retro style as a justification for its quality, but that doesn't mean it's not worth mentioning. The music is catchy and fitting for each stage, and the graphics are colorful and show off the wacky caracters and environments quite well.
-Humor. A minor thing, but this game is silly. Goofy characters and bad puns.
Cons:
-Challenging Gameplay. I know I praised the gameplay before, but I want you to remember that this game is hard, and it sometimes simply isn't fair. Sometimes you'll get punished for not having lightning-fast reflexes, other times you'll fall into a pit for trying to attack an enemy. Speakng of which, the instant-death in this game is incredibly prolific. Bottomless pits and spikes are abundant, and you are left with little to do about it other than die over and over until you get it right. Dying not only takes you back to one of the stage's infrequent checkpoints, but also causes you to lose gold, unless you can retrieve it.
Overall, great game. Buy it if you want a challenge.

More Megaman than even the PC port of Megaman is, without any of the negetive qualities associated with that one.  A great classic 2d game that harkens back to the NES days.  Absolutely must-play.  Think a Mario 3 style overworld where you move about on a pre-selected path and choose (usually from 2~3 different choices) which board to play next.  Each board is unique, with it's own graphics, punchy 8-bit music (you'll love it), and end-boss (who gives you new ABILITIES!).  It's just like Megaman, so if you enjoyed the NES days and want another new NES game with better controls, this is totally your calling.
You can even backtrack to a Zelda II (NES)-like town and go buy new cool stuff.
SECRETS GALORE so even Metroid fans won't be 'alienated' (okay, bad bad pun I know).
If your into retro-side-scrolling / platform jumping games, entirely a must-buy.
VERY well made,  10/10.
This goes on the list of must-have retro games:
AVGNA 1 & 2 (moar fun here if you like Shovel Knight and vice-versa)
Axiom Verge (I can't believe it's-not-metroid!)
AM2R (not on Steam, free community-made game, just like Metroid 2)
Artifact Adventure (dragon quest 3's long-lost twin!)
Dragon Fantasy (both - 1st one is said to be better)
Penny Arcade's Rainslick precipice of darkness 3 (almost like FF Mystic Quest/Chrono Trigger)
Retro City Rampage (8-bit 2d top-down GTA)
Rogue Legacy (this is really fun if you like rogue + 2d side-scrolling + level building)
Gnomoria (Simplified dwarf fortress in isometric 2d)
I am sure I may have missed a few, but hey, I still play SimTower on PC and Super Metroid on SNES... so what do I know, I am just some dumb mid-30s aged man.

Been using Magix 2016, while I did not Legitimately own the software it was a good consumer video converter.
Now having purchased MAGIX Video deluxe 2017 Plus Steam Edition. It has limited capabilities in short you can't get
newer plugins for effects from their store, as the only content is what you get with the purchase.
I've seen many negative reviews about the program itself freezing. The program is choosy with the container it wants to read I tested two HEVC encoded videos , one contained in .mkv and one contained in .mp4, it didn't want to export the mkv file resulting in a 2 minute freezing of the program.
Do I Recommend MAGIX Video deluxe 2017 Plus Steam Edition?
Yes, It's a cheap got it during Autumn Sale 2017 for $7.94 priced accordingly to my region.( Which made it more attractive as buying from the retail site would cost me more).
Now for the Bad Reviews I've been reading , Magix does it work and works as advertised.
Now A few problems arise that make the program confusing:
1) Why is this one cheaper than the other 2017 deluxe advertised on steam?
-I really don't know but according to the reply I got this one is the better version.
2) The program does not exit properly on steam, and the process remains in the task manager.
- Easily solvable by doing the following.
A.) Open the videodeluxe.ini, which you find under the following path:
C:\Users\*Username"\AppData\Roaming\MAGIX\Videodeluxe23_steam\
B.) Search for the section [MobileSync].
C.) Set [MobileSync] Flags=0 and save the videodeluxe.ini.
I don't know why they never bothered to patch a single digit change though in the program defaults.
In Summary:
Cheap and affordable.
Don't trust the bad reviews they are mostly early adopters who had have problems which were fixed in the latest patches.
You probably need to change some file formats for it to be read by the Movie Maker(Maybe use Handbrake).
There is also a steep learning curve take note of that.

While I loved the Act I, such a great mod, I can't say I'm satisfied with what Act II has to offer - and while I'm well aware it is still incomplete, I am nonetheless unsatisfied with the direction it's taking. You see, while assets are superb, though the assets are high quality and apart from the zombies (which looks like some store bought asset and not something native to game) are close to Act I's, just more vibrant, level design feels way worse. I'm not sure if this is some sort of "uncanny valley for environments" where more detailed environments with same design philosophies look worse, or just the Dev team recycling old ideas and cliches without much consideration, but the environments are way less convincing, more confusing, and full of absolutely generic puzzles such as "find a valve, then backtrack the area as it floods". Aesthetically environments aren't any better, the office building, and caves, and the tunnels feel like a rehash of Source mod, and are very dull, with office feeling like same room over and over, and the mines make no sense, lacking in any structural supports and being so close to surface while featuring minecarts and other heavy machinery. I would have given the devs some time to improve on the Act II before leaving a negative review, but considering level design and new shiny assets are the only notable aspects of game so far, with story yet to be told and enemies feeling like work in progress placeholders, and being quite mediocre and a step back from previous act, I genuinely doubt things will improve any further.

There is also the ability to play on different maps some are dependant upon the number of players. ( You can have 4! :D) There is the classic Archon map, maps that allow your guys to level up to level 3, and maps that have runes that provide benefits when you move onto them.
For those of you who feel the base game was fine the way it was however, and don't want all these additions. You are in luck as you have the ability to turn off the secondary abilities so it will play like the base game. In fact they even brought in the old school original Archon graphics for units, as well as updated graphics. The only drawback is the multiplayer is same computer only. No network/internet. Which hurts it IMO.

PROS:
► It's fun to play as both Innocent and Infected.
► You can apply different abilities to different characters (adds more mystery to the game).
► Most cosmetics are unlockable without having to pay for microtransactions.
► LAN games for when you have enough other people in the house who want to play the game and want to avoid the cancerous community.
► You can get tokens to unlock new outfits for your characters.
CONS:
► Graphics are always constant, regardless if you set them to low (which barely even reduces the texture quality).
► Partying lobbies will ruin your experience as they will usually just kill you off even if you ARE innocent.
► Queuing takes a while sometimes.
► You still get players from other parts of the world who don't speak your language playing in the same game.
► Some players will just loudly spam♥♥♥♥♥♥into their microphone during the character selection screen.
► You can't adjust the volume of other players' mics.
► The Werewolf Pack, which supposedly gives you an Infected character with different abilities, makes the game Pay-to-Win at this point.
MY OTHER OPINIONS:
I heavily dislike the fact that players can party up as it just incentivizes cheating and foul play within the party (like killing off players who aren't in their party). The game is fun if you have a group of chill friends to play this with. I heavily encourage playing with a friend or two because the game will be really depressing when you solo queue.
Due to the small community, you usually end up facing some of the same people over and over again. Typically, you'll usually get paired up with extremely competitive die-hard players who are just extremely toxic and have no fun. Most of the streamers who play this game are just as vulgar and irritating to PLAY with, much less WATCH.
Now, this game is constantly changing, which may seem great or terrible for others, so I didn't bother listing this as a pro or con for these reasons. Many of the balancing changes they make to the game are either broken for Innocents, Infected, or even both factions. The camera is just about the weakest weapon in the game that relies more on chance than range. I remember having to use the flash on an Infected 4 TIMES before I downed him.
Also, you have to be really quick with picking up items and ammo otherwise you're screwed. The other innocents don't really care if you make it out alive.
This game may be free-to-play now, but the developers were forced to go the free-to-play route due to the small fanbase.

Love it to bits.
I bought this on Xbox 360 last year and when I finished it the first time, I wasn't done playing so I started over again right away on apocalyptic mode and 100% completed it.
When I saw it on steam with Darksiders 2 I got both, currently playing Darksiders and loving it again. This time on apocalyptic mode without the Abyssal Armor.
I see a lot of people comparing it to God of War, a game I have only played one time for about 10-20 mins on a friends system, it didn't hook me like Darksiders.
To me Darksiders is just like Zelda: Ocarina of time (another great game that I have replayed multiple times) in a different theme.
Similarities;
Equipment:
-Earthcaller/Ocarina, makes sound to unlock passages.
-Shadowflight/chickens, similar gliding ability to get to otherwise unreachable areas.
-Crossblade/Boomerang, comes back to you, stuns enemies, hits switches.
-Tremor Gauntlet/Megaton Hammer, Silver and Golden Gauntlets, allows you yo destroy obstacles and move large objects that you couldn't before.
-Mercy/Bow, range weapon, not really unique, but still...
-Abyssal Chain/Hook-Shot, grapple onto something distant and pull yourself toward it.
-Mask of Shadows/Lens of Truth, lets you see and interact with things that are not normally visible to the naked eye.
-Ruin/Epona, a horsey with little tokens/carrots that you can spend to dash for a few seconds that replenish one by one after a few seconds.
-Vessels/Bottles that you can fill with life, chaos, wrath/mana or something that auto heals you when you die (Undying/Fairy's Spirit).
Other:
-Beams that you have to redirect with mirrors or portals
-Pushable blocks
bomb growth/flower that you pick up and throw and they blow up after a few seconds and regrow.
-Dungeon map and hoard seaker/compass in each level that shows locations of chests and boss room.
-Lifeshards/Pieces of Heart that turn into Life cores/Heart containers when you collect 4 of them
-Free Life cores/Heart containers after defeating each dungeon boss.
-Life cores/Heart containers
-You teleport out of the dungeon via a glowy blue circle after defeating the boss.
-An annoying companion that lives inside you somewhere and comes out to hover around your head and bug you about stuff (also helps you remember what to do next)
Improved mechanics:
you cant accidentally dash/dodge off of an edge and fall
you open chests quickly with no fanfare (except for the equipment/abilities)
no limit on currency capacity meaning no wasted cash chests when at max
you know whats in a chest by its appearance
quick summoning of your horsey
Extra mechanics:
Weapon leveling
Combo purchasing
weapon augmenting
So there are a lot of similarities, but that is no reason to criticize a game, in fact, that was the reason I was interested in it and partly why I like the game, because these items and mechanics are great fun to use and they work. I judge the game on weather it was fun and if it was well made, and it is.
The level design is great, when you have to backtrack in a dungeon you usually take a different path that was inaccessible going in.
The puzzles are good, the pacing of battles between puzzles is good, the progression of harder enemies is good, whenever you see an enemy for the first time it is treated like a mini-boss, you can learn its attacks and how to fight it and from then on its a regular enemy.
The animations are great especially when characters are talking, their facial expressions and lip/mouth movements match the speech and mood of the character, Vulgrim is a great example when he talks about souls or hearts you can see the emotion on his face even through all the teeth.
Fighting is fluid and easy to pull off combos and dodges in any direction at any time, you can interrupt almost any attack and go straight into a dodge, you can switch weapons on the fly and do combos with multiple weapons, if you are good, you can dodge almost any attack. killing enemies in different ways is satisfying and thank god there is no quick-time-events.
If Darksiders is a God of War clone, I will be looking into God of War in the near future.

As the Naruto series slowly comes to an end, I find myself saddened and desperately trying to find Naruto experiences that will help me relive the greatest moments from the manga and anime.  This is such a rich universe filled with loveable characters, epic battles, and awesome powers.  Utimate Ninja STORM Revolution brings the mythos and AWESOME to life at every step..  But there are opportunities.
First, I will warn you that the console versions still seem to be the way to go but this port is the best I've played so far.  We're all hopeful Storm 4 will deliver across the board but this game is no consolation prize.  What I love about this game is that it strikes a great balance between action/adventure game and deep fighter.  The exploration and questing is as satisfying as pulling off 60+ combos, calling in support, or pulling off an amazing block/comeback.
Replay value is a huge thing for me.  As a family man, I can't buy every game that comes out so, when I buy a game, it needs to provide tons of replay value and fun.  Revolution certainly fits the bill there.
Really, I love everything about this game.  It looks beautiful and the PC frame rate issues seem to have been resolved.  There are only a few things that bug me.  They are not deal breakers but it's good to know they are there:
1)  Loading Times - They feel too long for what the game is..  Sure, there is the open world component but loading between menus seems very archaic to me.  You may want to load this game onto your SSD, which I may very well do.  Mind you, my gaming rig is not a bleeding edge system but it is more powerful than the average PC so this should not be happening at all.
2)  Button Assignments - While you can remap buttons fully and controller support is flawless, I still don't get the button mappings in this series.  I feel that wasting a button for charging chakra is silly but I suppose it makes sense with the mechanic of chakra-loaded attacks.  A dedicated shuriken button, however, is really goofy.. But no biggy.  I would just rather see a weak/medium/strong setup for more control over your combos and fighting style; that way, people can't write this off as a mere button masher.
3)  Lock-On System - The 1v1 battles are still the best.  I love the concept of FFA/Battle Royale, but the lock-on system here still leaves something to be desired.  You click the analog stick to unlock and click again to lock on, but it's not always clear which target you will lock onto.  A simple fix would be to have the crosshair appear on your targets as you move your characters, then click to confirm the lock.  Easy.
Regardless, this game is tons of fun and it makes me want to go back to the XBox 360 and even Gamecube games.  That's not because this game sucks but, rather, it's so good you want to explore and revisit all the Naruto games.  I hope they make proper ports of all the games from previous platforms but, more importantly, I hope they make them proper ports, deserving of the PC platform.
Anyway, back to UNS Revolution...
One feature I absolutely LOVE is the Network Clone.  This is an avatar that battles online players while you are away from the game.  They pop up in other instances, collecting items and experience.  You can fully customize your Network Clone and Story/Ninja Tournament characters, which I love because this gives the unlockables even more value.
Ultimate Ninja Storm Revolution combines the best of breed technologies and game mechanics from games like Mystic Heroes, Dynasty Warriors, Dragon Ball-Z (the good ones, not Xenoverse), and Forza (i.e. driveatars).  Truly, this game is a treat.  If you're a fan, don't hesitate..  Though I will say it is better-suited at $40 or less, not $50.. At least on PC.
With regards to Ombre's review and similar write-ups, the Story/Campaign is not boring if you don't mind running around a bit and reading lots.  There is quite a bit of dialogue and not that much voice acting, which isn't a bad thing but it does make me feel that this is a licensed game that should have released at a more appealing price point since they did cut a few corners.
When you choose your "move type", you have to choose between Awakening (buffed character), Support Drive (buffed defense/attack support moves), or Ultimate Justu (unlocks OP ultimate).  I think this is actually a selling point for more casual players or folks like me, who can't dedicate as much time to gaming and certainly not one game in particular, no matter how much we love said game.  If you were able to have Awakening and Support Drive together, for instance, it'd be pretty OP..  And it would widen the gap between newer players and dedicated/hardcore vets.  That would make the experience too exclusive and essentially render the online gameplay useless.
Speaking of online, I have not played online with the exception of challenging a few Network Clones.  To that end, I felt really underpowered.  I landed tons more hits than my opponents and yet they still won.  The time you invest in this game unlocking things, leveling up, buying ninja tools, etc certainly does give you an edge.  The players I battled were level 30ish.  Battles do come down to skill but it's tougher when you are matched up against more seasoned players so that's something to keep in mind.
Overall, I would totally recommended this game.  I reiterate that this feels like more of a $40 game but there is tons of value there, regardless of the price point.  I recommend Revolution without hesitation if you love fighting games, anime, and/or Naruto but temper expectations just a little bit.  IF you're super picky, I'm sure you will find glaring flaws. =oP

Personal opinion: Get this game instead of Sacred 3 if you're looking for an Action RPG!
My first impression playing this game back in 2010 was pretty special. I started a Dryad (hey, they looked hot and I love Druids) and watched the fairly epic cinematic, after which I was placed on a beach with a kind of a mentor beside me. I guess the gods didn't smile upon him on that day though, because somehow I ended up having to tutor myself. First thing I noticed when gaining control was the graphics. One word. Wow. They are incredible, and the attention to detail is pretty much un-parallelled. Leaves being side swept, a little bird making his nest - hundreds of small things that leave you with a warm and fuzzy feeling inside. Even now in 2014, it still looks great.
I still have that Dryad - but I specced her so badly that she is broken beyond repair. I
recommend using the Sacred 2 Wiki for help with builds. There is no respec option, and if you find yourself wanting to play it all the way to Niob, your spec pretty much needs to be perfect.
The sound is good as well, although the voice acting is bad. Not terribad but bad enough that you treasure the fact that only the main quests have voiced dialogue.
Moving on; most of the classes in the game are innovative and fresh. Whoever saw an ancient Egyptian-inspired Anubis-like robot thingie before as a class? Packing an alien blaster along with his hammer no less. Very fresh, very fun. You diversify a bit by choosing a god and one of two campaigns (good or evil), which adds a good deal of replayability. Rather annoyed by the fact that you can't select gender for the classes though. Some years ago I never touched any female class, for some reason. Thankfully I outgrew it, or I would have missed out on half of this game.
The story is fairly weak, but the focus doesn't really lie there either, as it gives you hundreds of side quests left and right. In fact there are so many, I find myself skipping half of them. Many of them are kind of like MMO quests in a sense. Very generic; a silly story behind it and mediocre rewards. But it works, somehow. In one early side quest though, you are pitted against the game's first boss. This was a pleasant surprise - as once you engage a boss monster, the camera centers on the boss and the game spits out some cool music. He took a serious pounding too, so it was a good moment.
The map is gigantic; as far as I know it has the biggest world in an action RPG, ever. I have still not explored everything after well over 100 hours of play (played it on a disc version most of the time), and there are several optional bosses where you can see how good (or bad) your build is. Bosses can be incredibly punishing, but they are also a lot of fun. Keep your thumb on the spacebar.
The difficulty level when playing Bronze is extremely easy the first 2-3 hours. I considered re-starting several times and selecting Silver instead. But it's gotten more challenging. This really depends on the class and spec you want to play. I have one character in Platinum; a Seraphim, and I still find the class a lot of fun. I have chosen to spec her both with Sword / Shield and Ranged (for BeeEffGee). This'll likely hurt me quite a bit if I reach Niob, but for now it works well. I like being able to change things up now and then.
Multiplayer is dead, unfortunately. Seems Ascaron went and got themselves bankrupt, and was forced to shut down their US servers. EU servers still worked when I started playing it back in 2010, but I believe they are shut down as well.
All in all though, great game. Sort of a diamond in the rough but if you can see past some bugs, crashes and general hiccups, you may find yourself in love with this game, like me. I've played it for about 120 hours; I am on my third version of the game now, and after experiencing just one in-game crash in 14 hours of playing, I can finally, after many years, recommend this game. On the previous versions it probably crashed between 2-300 times in 100 hours of playing.
Since I wrote the review the game has crashed 7 times in 28 hours of play. Still not too bad, considering I've had PhysX enabled all that time.

Saints Row: The Third is an over the top, open world over the shoulder third person shooter with strong action, good controls and some over sexualized comedy. There are plenty of giant purple bats, leather clad dancers, and awkward situations all done for the sake of comedy. You play as the head of a gang from the start, but really its a group of three tight friends that grows bigger to include a giant powerhouse, an ex FBI tech geek, a pretensions actor, a serious turncoat twin and an auto tuned pimp. These aren't just quest givers, you can call on them to help you on missions. When they're with you, they're smart enough to find cover in gun fights, take hostages and even steal a car to follow you when you drive off without them. When your "homies" fall, you need to pick them back up or lose the mission. There are frequent checkpoints, but with a game so fun, I don't mind if I die.
The franchise really took a step away from being just a lesser version of Grand Theft Auto. They upped the gameplay and the comedy. Where GTA 4 turned gritty and real, Saints Row went the silly fun route. You can take hostages to use them as human shields. Improve your aim by crouching down. Head shot any enemy for an instant kill. Otherwise the enemies will spin around hoping to find cover and forcing your aim to follow them. There are multiple flying take downs and the animation seems outstanding for something that has so many of them.
There is so much customization too. Everything from customizing your own look, to creating how your gang looks. If you want all thugs, go for it. If you want all space men or strippers. That's up to you. Their stats aren't affected. Its all just a look. Having your crew around makes an interesting mission even more fun. The whole thing is streamlined. Go to your PDA that will get a phone call sending you to a location on your GPS to start the mission. You'll find a wide variety in missions, fly to this location, take out a bunch of gang members, hop in a turret, drive through hostile territory, jump out of a plane ..... in a tank and shoot at people and other tanks as you fall. Then hop in a virtual world with a new weapon. Its always interesting and a few missions take place outside of the city in their own unique environments.
Some missions end with a choice that really adds replay value. Do you get a one time sum of cash, or do you want a constantly generating smaller sum of cash. Do you want the aide of someone new or keep someone old? Even down to trivial things like discounts on car upgrades vs discounts on weapon upgrades or who you let live.
The city of Steelport is a bright, beautiful, vibrant and gritty city. It all depends what area you're in. The industrial zone has no lights, while the tourist part has beautiful neon lights. The city really lights up at night and looks amazing while flying. As the game progresses, the sights change. You'll see a sunken aircraft carrier, a plane tail up and much more to remind you of just how you've affected the city.
Since this is a new city, you'll need to take it over. How do you do that? Participating in side quests like racing cars or a turf war with one of the three rival gangs in the city. You can buy stores that count to the take over percentage. There are even score based games like insurance fraud and mayhem that have you rag dolling into cars or destroying property. When you own a percentage of the city, you'll make money for it every real life hour you play. Outside of controlling the city, you can participate in assassinations, car thefts and hijackings with a passenger, then hold them until you get a ransom.
Money for weapons becomes irrelevant. You'll always have more than enough ammo even if you never visit a gun store. What the money really goes to are upgrades. In the PDA menu you'll upgrade how much ammo you can have, what guns your crew has, your total health, how fast it regenerates, how much stamina you have and so much more. This is the expensive part of the game. Each gun has four levels of upgrade. The fourth level is always something silly like explosive bullets from a pistol.
There are plenty of weapons in six major types, melee, small, sub machine guns, shot guns, assault rifles, misc (rockets), sniper rifles and four types of throwable things like grenades. You can only have one of each weapon type equipped at a time, but that's more than enough. Some missions require you to use a rocket launcher and it won't just give you a launcher, it gives you unlimited rockets. Its one of the joys of this game. High powered weapons with big effects. Once the STAG army shows up, there are some even more creative weapons like a force rifle that when used it pushes away enemies and fully charged obliterates them. There's just so much variety here, even a tactical missile strike, but that's not nearly as fun as everything else.
Bosses are big brutes that can run right through you. They are pretty simple to take down though. Shoot them enough times and a quick button prompt will finish them off. The ones without guns will throw cars and benches around. The ones with guns carry flame throwers or heavy machine guns that thankfully jam. With them gone you can pick up their heavy weapons to use as your own, but the bigger the weapon, the slower you move. These weapons are worth the time for the power and fun they bring, especially the sticky bomb launcher.
On top of that, you can climb into vehicles, cars, motor cycles, trucks, but better than that are tanks, armored SUVs, helicopters and some futuristic hover jets and cycles. The hover jets and cycles have two modes, jet and hover. Its perfect from a gameplay standpoint, go fast or hover so you can easily take out slow moving ground units and land on a dime. The vehicles with weapons are a lot of fun to shoot with unlimited ammo, but there are cool downs. Tanks that pancake cars. Missiles that lock onto things and follow them. Its very enjoyable.
The characters in your crew are excellently voiced and your chemistry together really shines through. Sure they poke fun at one another, but they have some memorably fun times beyond just shooting things. Silly happy moments like singing to Sublime on the radio and Oleg revealing how he has met his intellectual equal while in a firefight. The bosses of the gangs are worthy characters in their own right. They really make cut scenes interesting.
With you playing a criminal and all, there is notoriety in stars. The cops won't just chase after you, but the gangs and STAG army will too. Police will send helicopters with snipers. Enemy gangs will even setup roadblocks to stop you. It gets to a chaotic level sometimes when a gang and an army are after you. All three factions including your own start to fight in giant wars that can have dozens of people. Its amazing to be a part of. The game makes good use of big environments so you can flank your enemies and they can flank you.
Saints Row: The Third is an amazing and fun game with enough DLC to choke Godzilla. Its mostly all just cosmetic stuff. The Complete Pack has been $5, there's no reason not to pick it up, but with its comedy, its just not for kids.

Short Review:
All in all, the game is nice fun in short spurts, which is in my humble opinion an important aspect of an endless runner. Montaro fulfills that, and by requiring the costumes to be unlocked in order, also satisfies what I believe to be the most important goal, an addictive element. Here, it’s presented as the next thing a person can purchase, and all the player has to do is play the game. Like it or not, the player will earn doge coins and be able to purchase more costumes. But the player will likely like it, and be the next thing he or she looks forwards to. It was for my girlfriend, at least, who is definitively better at Montaro than me.
Long Review:
I don’t know if this game is available on mobile, but it should be. Purchased on steam, the only button to press is clicking the mouse, which makes the main character, a doge, jump. Despite the ostensibly boring controls, the game presents a number of simple challenges that might better be thought of as a series of short neverending challenges, includes cats that must be dodged as well as those that don't. The further along the doge runs, the more complicated these challenges become as they vary in frequency and placement.
The main character excels in cuteness, as he is a doge. The overall potential cuteness of the game is probably lost on some of its potential audience, however, in that one of the resources for the dog to collect in order to complete his challenges are panties. Simply put, the doge must get panties to be able to bounce off of bananas to defeat the challenges and continue his endless running.
Earning doge coins is not the actual objective of the endless runner, as the objective is to keep running, but they are earned along the way. These coins let you purchase costumes for doge that increase in price. My only complaint about the game rests here, stemming from the requirement that a player must unlock one costume to get the one after one. The requirement is not my complaint, but the last costume is. Namely, I feel it inferior to at least the six costumes preceding it.

It was a dark and storm night. No, really. I just wanted some stickers, and I had to get an achievement in order to do the last one for the day. I've played Fatal Frame, Dead Space, I habitually watch horror movies in the dark with surround sound or headphones. So, needless to say, I am not exactly a novice when it comes to the area that is horror. The subject of this game is something that preys upon a lot of peoples inner most fears. Being alone, playing on the computer, and something bad happens.
I was having a gay ol time; I feel it appropriate to use that particular turn of phrase as the last thing I was reading in this game....well we'll get to that. The game starts out and doesn't look anything special. Not top shelf graphics, but we aren't playing NES either. You sit in front of a computer and go through a tutorial. Pretty easy stuff, though I wonder why anyone leaves a window open and every light of their house on. It's night, I'm in the dark, windows closed, and I have at least one firearm within reach.
The character you play, is some dude/dudette (no need to be sexist) and you find out that you have to go through various sites to put together a key to find a murder room on the deep web. I've watched a few horror movies with similar themes and wasn't the least bit bothered. Now, you get warned at the end of the tutorial that there is some "breather" out there killing people that don't keep their door closed, or hitchhikers. I scoffed at how cheesy that sounds. What kind of premise is this? Dude gives up if he can get past your front door? I spend a few minutes looking around and realize, you sit smack dab between two rooms, and there is a big window open right in front of you and a bit to the side. I always think about worst case scenerios, so the logistics of this doesn't fly. But, when in Rome... or Tuscaloosa.
So the trick is to find 8 parts of a key to see some death. I'm down, and start clicking. First few don't work. Apparently some only work at certain times? Idk. So I go to a confession site, and it works. I laugh and screen shot some messed up confessions. Having a good time. I think I hear something, back out and look around. I turn off the light and the computer goes off too. No surfing in the dark, and apparently the dark fools your very not dedicated killer. Nothing happens, so I go back and I post a confession from my youth. Tried to think of the worst thing I've done, it wasn't horrible, at least compared to what was otherwise posted. I'm curious if other peoples confessions get uploaded. Most would probably just make up some weird stuff for the lolz, but I'm a genuine person. I was in the spirit of the game.
More dead rooms, and I'm on day 4. Where the time went, I do not know. All I know is my cell in game rings when I'm reading confessions. True to his name, he sits there breathing. I listen for a few, make a joke askins if he needed some tissues, even though he can't hear me. Haha. Good times. Hang up, back to reading confessions. Seconds later he calls again. I'm a little less eager this time and I answer. Mr Dirty is at it again, but I hang up and shut off the lights. I sit there for a couple minutes thinking, "gd it's dark". My room is dark, my game is dark. I thought I hear something again and I can't tell if it came from my game or real life.
I wait a couple minutes, then decide that should be sufficient. Turn stuff on and jump back to finding sites. More that don't work. Then I find this Grandmother site... Oh grandma... This is why I made the joke bout having a "gay time", as granny was busy...well, I'll let you learn that on your own. Suffice it to say, I was laughing, repulsed, and a little turned on. I blame the idea of the pizza. I swear I hear something again, so I turn around and see nothing. It sounded like someone fuqing with my door. My character runs to the front door and I stand there. I find you can push a button to look around. Don't ask me the button, the last couple minutes of the game are a blur.
I look around outside feeling a lot less amused. My bi-curious boner has turned into a fear boner. Least that will keep me from peeing myself, I think as I try to keep myself from letting things get out of control. Now, I suffer from anxiety. I have always had one of those imaginations where I walk by a window in a dark room and always have this lingering fear in the back of my mind, that decades of horror movies have skull fuqed in there, that someone is going to be standing there, watching. I look out the window again, nothing going on. Looks like everywheresville.
I sit back at the computer and find another page to read. More that won't open, but one that will that didn't before. This "doctor" page where they do bad things to people. Then I read another about webcams they have hijacked so you can spy on people. There's another fear, thanks Steve Jobs. I notice a thing about buying access, and I don't know if you have money in game? but I open the games notepad to write down the address to email the dudes...
This is the culmination of all the years waiting for that face to appear in the window. The person in the dark with the snearing smile before they break in. Only its in the game, but my brain doesn't register. I go from about to type out an address, to being spun around and this face is inches from mine. Jesus spagetti monster tiddy fuqing christ on crutches. I shouted! I was so startled, my whole body jumped and my hand went for my .357. I've never yelled at a game before, never had one brain fuq me so hard. I went from laughing, to suddenly worrying if I♥♥♥♥♥♥myself. I couldn't hear what he said as I was busy shaking covering my mouth and looking around my computer monitor to where my door is; fully expecting someone to be there. I immediately closed the game and came to write this.
I don't know if the scare will work the next time I play, but I might wait a little while before I try again.  13/10, would shoot my bookcase out of fear from an imaginery killer again.

I used to play CivIV for years, logging hundreds of hours. I thought about buying it for Steam as well, but stumbled upon the deal for CivV instead - and purchased it. Sorry to say, it didn't feel like IV at all, so now I've purchased the IV as well.
IV is definitely more complex - you have a lot of details to worry about, there is tons of micromanagement (the city you completely forgot about for 22 turns has developed unhappiness because they demand Emancipation etc). But this is precisely how it mimics the "real world" and captivates the powerlessness that you need to urge yourself to play just another turn.
I like the diplomacy mechanism. I like the different automation options for the workers. I like the health aspect in the cities. In fact, I like most things about the game, with only one exception - combat. Now this is something that can be really frustrating - imagine defending your city with SAM infantry and it is being brought down by a heap of ancient era warriors. Not cool.
But overall, a very enjoyable experience, the vanilla Civ IV is better that CIv V complete, EXCEPT the combat system. To be honest, it all boils down to Baba Yetu...

There are some excellent elements in the action RPG Sacred 2, but they are overshadowed by several serious problems.  The character classes are interesting, the progression choices to customize your character's operation are superb, itemization is good, and the world is large.  As for the bad: it is extremely tedious to find and travel to quest objectives which is made worse by several related bugs.  It is difficult to select targets, even with a PC mouse.  The isometric view is more top-down than a looking-ahead view angle; this hampers navigation and prevents you from seeing and targeting enemies.  The game lacks a tutorial to introduce game elements, though I was able to eventually figure most things out through trial and error.  I spent about six hours with this game, but I'll be uninstalling and will not return.

I picked this game up as part of a Humble Bundle and as such had no expectations to fulfil.  Essentially it's a Diablo clone, it's quite long at around 30 hours to complete the single player campaign - and that's with skipping the DLC islands and pretty much skipping the side quests from chapter three onwards.  It's a big old game, I'd uncovered about half the map before I stopped playing.  I hit level 41 by the time I finished it, max level is 200 (though that is only achieveable on subsequent playthoughs at a higher difficulty level)
The comabt etc gets very repetitive fairly quickly, as there is no penalty on using the plentiful healing potions you gather - your main risk of dying is from not paying attention rather than any sort of tactical challenge.
My main complaint with this game is the extremely complex mechanics and poor help/documentation that go with it.  Half the challenge in this game is understanding what mechanics interact with each other and what gear is best to use.  One example; I initially took the swords skill (one of ten slots you get, I unlocked 8 in my playthrough) and invested a bunch of points in it - I then took dual-wield; expecting that dual-wielding swords would provide double the bonus as it does in most other RPGs.  Instead I found that the moment you equip two weapons, all points in the sword skill are wasted and only the dual-wield skill provides a bonus.
If you min-max and read the (limited) guides on the internet this does become clear - but nothing in the game even hints at this.
Played through as a Seraphim "Exalted Warrior" character, if you get it cheaply and like the Diablo/Torchlight genre of games then you'll get a solid couple of days playtime out of this I reckon.
There's lots to do, but its not a very deep game - it's mostly just hack and slash with courier/kill sidequests thrown in.  A special mention goes to the NPC AI, your companions which some missions have you babysit, are the most suicidal folks you'll ever come across - they constantly run in the wrong direction pulling vast swathes of enemies and dying - I gave up on any escort missions after the first chapter.
A great game if you have friends to play it with. I've enjoyed every moment of playing it! :D

There are a lot of ARPGs on the market. Like Diablo, Torchlight, Titan Quest or Divine Divinity but is Sacred 2 worth you time?
Well, if you really like the genre then this game won't dissapoint you. It might not suit everybody but it sure as hell is a solid title that has been under the rader. This game has a somewhat weird character with oddball humor, it doesn't take itself to seriously but that's not a bad thing.
The best aspects of the game are the huge gameworld filled with numerous interesting sidequests, explorable areas and tons of loot. There are many hidden areas filled with treasures that can be discovered by you. There are many monsters and npcs scattered around the world. There is so much loot and equipement to find that it will keep you occupied for quite a while. You can choose from 7 classes that all feel really unique and look incredible. The combat is pretty standard but nevertheless really rewarding, furthermore leveling up your character is really addictive. The level system with the skills and abilities is quite unique and somewhat refreshing, despite being a bit confusing at first. Overall it just feels like a really solid game and you get a lot of content for your money.
Although there are some negative sides of game like the general lack of polish, sometimes the game feels a bit unpolished and could be a bit better in some parts. The interface and controls are really unintuitive and needs some work in order to completely master them. The graphics look georgeous but it's pretty bright and can be quite distracting, but that's more of a personal preference. The voice acting is really mediocre but it somewhat adds to the flavour, the story isn't to special and if you look for an epic adventure this game won't really satisfy your needs.
If you're looking for a great rpg with tons of content and equipement to gather, this is the right game. There is so much to do in this game that it will require you a lot of time. The start is a bit slow but after a while the game gets really addictive.

[Description]
Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege is a first-person multiplayer shooter that borrows from Counter Strike and hero shooters, mixing it together into a tactical, objective-based shootout where movement is slow and combat is fast. The game features asymmetrical gameplay where the teams are not always balanced in their abilities. Heavy emphasis is put on procedural environmental destruction allowing players to break certain structures by planting explosives, or shooting walls to make bullet holes or even larger ones to climb through.
[Pros]
+ Over 30 operators to choose from, based on real life counter terrorism units, each with their own unique weapons and gadgets.
+ No match will be the same thanks to the diverse cast of characters which is still getting expanded by Ubisoft, even 1.5 years after the game’s release.
+ Precise procedural destruction of most of the games floors and walls resulting in a tactical shooter like no other; simply running and gunning will only get you so far
+ Customization options for guns which also impact the way they operate. From a simple silencer to four different sights and weapon grips or fore grips, everything will change weapon behavior.
+ Pleasing graphics that look great and don’t require a monster PC to push 60 FPS or higher.
+ A fair use of micro-transactions where you can only buy skins and operators with real money but you can also unlock them through in-game currency.
+ You just can’t buy anything that gives you an advantage over other players.
+ Season pass owners get 1 week early access to new operators and all new operators in that year for free along with other skins and small benefits.
+ Maps are free for everyone, it doesn’t matter if you bought the season pass or not, everyone can play together.
+ Incredible sound engine that lets you hear precise enemy movement, like them walking into glass on the floor and other surfaces, or the exact direction where the steps are coming from. This is making good use of 5.1 surround sound or just good stereo headphones.
+ Music is fitting the game’s tone very well you just don’t hear much of it since it is only playing at the beginning and at the end of rounds which in turn is making you not really care for it all.
[Cons]
- Lag compensation, netcode and tickrate is still broken and you sometimes die out of nowhere while your enemy could clearly see you. (This is being worked on and hopefully fixed in the near future)
- Multiplayer against other players or against AI are the only two modes, there is no campaign which I think is a missed opportunity.
- Steep learning curve that can be very frustrating for beginners since regular players of the game will know exactly what walls can be shot through, what angles work best and how to quickly peek corners to make the best use of the sometimes broken netcode.
- Unlocking operators with in-game currency can take a long time based on your willingness to spend time with the game and how good you are. Just stay away from the starter edition or the game will be even more grindy since each base operators cost much much more than they normally would and you will be unable to upgrade to the standard edition once you bought the starter.
[Conclusion]
While this iteration of the series is vastly different than it’s predecessors, I think it’s a solid addition to the series. Rainbow Six Siege is very unique in what it does and we have yet to see a game like it. I recommend it to fans of SWAT 4, Insurgency, and generally anyone who enjoys or is interested in tactical first person games where you have to be cautious of your surroundings, be aware of your enemies abilities, and a strong emphasis on teamwork.

Rome: Total War. So much can be said about this game. For this review I'll feel more comfortable explaining all of the Pro's and Con's I faced when playing this game. Remember, reviews are very subjective so my experience may not match yours. However, that shouldn't discourage you to purchase this title.
Pro's: Right off the bat I'm going to talk about one of the key selling points to this game. The Battles!
Battles in this game highly depend on your strategical and logical thinking. You command hundreds to thousands of soldiers on the battle field. Each having unique properties and abilities. Some troops are purely Missile (Troops that use Bows, Slings and Human Heads), while other troops can be a mix of this. A good example to look at are Skirmishers. These troops throw spears and damage units. When they're ammunition is depleted they go into combat with daggers and swords. However, they are inexperienced at hand to hand combat. These types of setbacks and advantages are what bring out the strategic aspect of Total War. So many possibilities as to how you can fight. It's definitely a well made and balanced system.
The Campaign!
Rome 1 has a phenominal campaign alongside its battles. The campaign map spans from Portugal to the Middle East and Russia. Northern Africa and the UK are also included. There are 21 factions however, only a couple are playable. The only way you can play as other factions is by easilly editing a certain script in Rome 1's files. I reccomend doing this as it gives you more options and various ways to make the campaign different. Each faction owns settlements in their unique areas. These can be profited off of to fund your army and other buildings to improve your empires happiness and what you can train in certain settlements. For example, the Carthaginians have access to War Elephants. These beasts can tear through any troop easilly. The only problem is you can't train them during early game as you need certain stables to do so.
Cons: The AI!
First of all, let me explain my position on the AI, It's not terrible at all, especially for a game made in 2004. However, it still needs to be adressed. In a game with a battle system that is dependant on strategy, well programmed AI is essential for such a mechanic. The AI in this game does fail to do so at times. Keep in mind though, the amount of times that such a problem occured is very miniscule. During sieges my Cavalry would sometimes decide to take the least logical route to get a to a certain point. Instead of going through an easy passage, they go to where all my infantry is and try to run through the hoardes of enemies. As long as you can correct them (Which can be done with one right click) this wont be a huge problem but, timing in Total War plays a big part in strategies. It may seem like I am nitpicking but, once you play this game you'll understand the importance of the AI.
Final Verdict: Do I recommend this game? ♥♥♥♥ yeah I do! This game is amazing and I will always love it to death. Especially considering how it was made in 2004. In fact, I would even say that this game out performs Rome 2 (That game is a huge mess that I don't care to explain right now).
I give this game 10 Roman Soldiers outta ♥♥♥♥ing 10. Also keep in mind, this comes with an expansion pack.

So, I purchased this game back in early 2011, and maybe played a few minutes before getting distracted by some new-and-shiny early-access zombie-survival title of a sort back then.
It's been over six years, and I started playing once more. This game is amazing. Most of the classes and maps are easy-to-learn, hard-to-master, while the non-cosmetic items and weapons provide a multitude of subclasses and playstyles to experiment with.
Plenty of maps and gamemodes included, with community servers providing custom maps and gamemodes. It's nice to have a competitive multiplayer FPS that you aren't meant to take too seriously in most cases. I have just as much fun goofing off as I do winning, unlike CSGO or something where winning is usually the only way to enjoy the game.
The community is still large, especially considering this game's age. We still get (free!) updates, and you can play the game entirely without making a single purchase. Alternatively, spend $0.10 on a skin, and unlock the premium features. Drops are a good way to earn a little extra cash, or trade up if you're patient enough for that sort of thing.
If you haven't played TF2 before, you owe it to yourself to give it a try.
