Sacred 2 is a Diablo-style action RPG set in a truly massive world. Its largest selling point is probably just that – this game is almost excessively huge. Sacred 2 features an incredible world packed with nearly 600 quests and a sprawling map that you’ll be unlikely to have seen even a quarter of in 20 hours. Every building is able to be entered (many with multiple floors), every NPC speaks, and most containers have loot stashed away in them. As typical of the genre, Sacred 2 offers multiple difficulties to unlock for even more replayability.
Looting is another huge draw – practically every enemy will drop loot, all with different stats and colorations. If one enemy doesn’t drop anything, you’ll soon have another 10 or more on screen anyway. Monsters, animals, and humanoids alike creep in every corner, waiting to swarm your character. To cope with this, you’re given a wide range of distinctly different player characters, each with an array of different armor, weaponry, special moves, and unique mounts (although all may buy horses as well).
Combat is fast, though oftentimes mindless, fun. No matter the character, you’re always open to many ways to play, from magic, to ranged, to multiple forms of melee (sword & shield, dual wielding, axes, clubs, etc.). Your mount, whether unique to your class or a horse, also opens up another combat style with its own unique stats and, for some, attacks. Enemies range from normal humans to mythical beasts such as harpies and werewolves, each with variations in stats, attacks, and appearances, guaranteeing you’ll have plenty of new monsters to slay your entire journey.
Sacred 2’s saving grace to the argument of it being “just another clone” is that it’s already fully aware of being a clone filled with various clichés. The game doesn’t take itself seriously; one moment you have men in bunny suits attacking you, another moment you’re fending off mutated sheep who’ve decided you should be food instead. Sacred 2 plays on its light-hearted silliness with quests such as those, jokes galore (cemeteries house plenty in particular), and fourth wall breaking moments – for instance, the Seraphim is fully aware she can’t proceed without the player and will make her grievances known quite vocally if you leave her standing alone for a short while. This both saves it from coming across as a simple clone and gives it plenty of character of its own.
It has its flaws, like all games. The biggest irritant might possibly be its camera, which attempts to be both isometric and standard 3rd person at the same time, often leading to it spiraling around awkwardly. Another point to make is not necessarily a flaw, but could be a massive turn off for some: the bright colors, voice acting, and purposeful ridiculousness of Sacred 2 could easily put off someone looking for a serious RPG, or possibly come across as poor quality before it becomes more apparent the game is using its clichés as a joke.
Overall, I’d happily recommend it to fans of Diablo style games, particularly those who love to explore, as you’ll have a lot to see, and hours and hours of combat-filled gameplay. Sacred 2 is truly an overlooked gem.

It was better than I expected, but definitely not as good as it's competitors such as Torchlight II or Path of Exile (though I'll admit I haven't played Diablo 3). The animation is subpar, and the combat doesn't have quite the punch that Torchlight has. The RPG systems are pretty good once you understand them, but they're a little confusing at first. Where it does shine is it's ludicrously large world map, non-linear structure, and mood. You'll probably notice in the above screenshots that this game is....over the top, to be nice. But rather than try and take itself seriously like most ridiculous medieval fantasy RPGs do, it's all very light hearted and silly, which works very well. The game would be really just stupid if it wasn't for the fact that the game KNOWS that it's stupid. The embracing rather than resisting of tropes saves this game from being an crappy Diablo rip off and instead gives it a tiny niche to fill, combining the action of Torchlight with the scope of the Elder Scrolls, failing slightly but not completely and succeeeding enough but not very much at both. 5/10, will probably complete and even play through multiple times.

Just finished a 10 hour session after downloading this game. So far I'm really enjoying myself. Despite the sheer fun of it though, there are some good and bad points.
The Good:
1. Looks decent for a title that's just a little over 3 years old. Reminiscent of the graphics you'd get from WoW at the same point in time.
2. Has a really low performance cap, so even on an older machine it'll run really well and be smooth.
3. The Combat is pretty fun, this is essentially a melee combo hack and slash game with a little bit of ranged via the crossblade to mix things up a touch.
4. Some of the puzzles are challenging but not insurmountable - the same can be said for a few of the boss fights.
5. The story (thus far) has been really engaging and I actually care about what's going to happen next.
The Bad:
1. As a console port, playing this on keyboard and mouse can be tricky as the controls don't lend themselves very well to some of the mechanics (primarily the ranged aspect of the game) If you've got an xbox controller, I'd suggest using it, if not, prepare to be frustrated with some of the reflex challenges posed by the default layout... You'll probably find yourself opening up the Steam overlay when you really don't need it (died several times on the first significant boss thanks to that)
2. The menu layout is pretty sparse and awkward to actually get into (you have to open your inventory in game to get to what few settings there are). Also when you decide to quit out, you are then returned to the oprning splash screen with a prompt to press enter to start... There is no straight up quit to desktop option which to me is an irritant.
Final Verdict:
I'd say pick it up of you're looking for something with a little of pace. The controls, although dodgy with the default keybinds can be remapped, so it's something that can be worked around and the gameply is really enjoyable.

This game is the highpoint of the total war franchise and the highpoint of turn-based/RTS hybrids.
What makes this game especially great is that the player has to manage population, distance and the economy to effectively expand their empire. This is the case with all total war games but it is especially important with Rome I. Cultural divisions and population density require Roman players to use auxiliaries and require players to reinforce their Roman Cohorts in the populous Italian core. Having an advanced economy is necessary to to equip legions with good equipment, maintain trade and fund schooling for future administrators and generals. Small armies have to be formed so fight brigands and main armies need to either be cycled through a modern populous city to reinforce or rely on auxiliaries to maintain their strength. Every aspect of managing an empire is at play and managing the growth of the country and the integration of people is something that requires effort rather than something that can be ignored and dealt with through just winning battles.
The battles of Rome are the most fast-paced and this makes them the most exciting. The game also has a treasure trove of mods that is still growing.

The way I see it, the game has a lot of potential and there are some well done things in the game, but they are left in the shadows of the negative things in this game. Unfortunely. So, let's get to the review:
(Short version is BEFORE THE summary at the bottom.)
They are good for a Unity game, considering it's just one guy (I assume) who made these all by himself (I assume), I really mean it. I've seen worse. Much worse. Not much to talk about here. Apart from random stuttering and lag in some locations where a lot of stuff is going on, even off-screen. Something Unity is good at in the hands of unexperienced/unseasoned user of Unity. Obviously we've all seen worse optimization, even in AAA games.
Well, we get all the sound effects you might expect: punch, hit, monster idle sounds, etc. There is no ambient music though, so just put on some Mambo #5 and you're good to go. However, the music when you find a temple, or an altar, the music is... intriguing... it adds to the atmosphere of this... mysterious story. That's pretty good. The music in the main menu sounds generic though.
Weeeellll... it's kinda boring. I was hoping for a little more (like everybody else I guess), like you know: you can get a clan of bears, upgrade your cave to hold more bears, go out with your bear-clan and kick some bottoms, fight other bear-clans far away, etc, etc.
Unfortunely, nothing like that here. It would be ok, IF the monsters you fight against would respawn, so it wouldn't be so empty when you kill everything. Yes, the monsters die forever, just like the food you ate disappers forever, so if you're suddenly low on stamina/health and you've killed/ate everything... too bad.
BUT, this killing/eating is tied to progression of you bear. You kill/eat something, your attributes get upgraded. This is where it got in the wrong direction. It would be a smarter decision to make the Bear Points your experience and you can spend Bear Points to upgrade your attributes. That way, you could make stuff respawn, so players could kill them again and get more Bear Points to upgrade other attributes. By making mobs/food add attributes themselves, removes that possibility, because players could just come back to the same mob and kill it over and over to upgrade their jump skill. So the Bear Points have been rendered useless. Unless you care about 2x damage, which doesn't do anything. Still takes about 3 hits to kill a fox. Upgrade strength, then it takes 2. So yeah, Bear Points = useless. They could be experience that you spent on attributes/perks, but unfortunely no.
The combat seems a bit broken. I hit an animal, it immidietly hits me back. Twice. No way to dodge either. Sometimes it works, but sometimes dodging doesn't work even when you're standing behind the monster. It's hard to explain this unless you've played it, but believe me it's terrible. The hit detection is very shoddy too. I point at the monster, right at his heart/head, it misses 50% of the time, whilst they hit you twice per your hit and almost never miss.
When you sleep in the bed, you can choose to sleep until day or night. Apart from changing day to night and night to day, it changes the mobs to different ones. Also, some events/monsters appear/happen only during the night or day, so you'll be doing a lot of back-and-forth from location to location.
HOWEVER... The story, is VERY intriguing. There is something eerie to the story, about... some ancient bears. The story, this... mysteriousness is awesome. It really is. Combined with that strange music when you find the temples is just... a great combination. This is a very strong positive thing to this game. I loved it and that's what kept me playing for... IDK, 12 hours? Of course the combat was annoying and when I killed/ate most of the things it got pretty boring.
Well, the models actually look good, especially the bear. The animations are also done well, but the animation for differnet actions, doesn't match up with the speed coded for those actions, so you can see the rabbit moving his legs really fast, but then you look how far he moved and it's just a few centimeters from you. It looked like he would put like a 20 second gap between us, but no.
One of the more annoying non-aggressive mobs has to be THE DUCKS. They take off like a F-16 or something. And like I mention: hit detection is not good, so it's hard to hit them. Also, all the mobs that fight back are annoying too. Why? Read TEH GAMEPLAY.
I don't think there's anything else to talk about.  Oh no wait, collectibles. They are there and some of them are useful, others... not so much. Useful: those for the bear, like a bed or a new skin/hat (bear with hats? That's cool). Not-so-useful: the ones for your cave. They don't seem to be doing anything. Except the bed. I also got... a cat that doesn't move or meow, a cat bed, some hats, a different skin and a new bed. I don't know much, because I still haven't finished this game. Surprisingly, this is a very long game, if you want the 100%.
The locations could be unlocked if you had enough Bear Points or level (if Bear Points were actually useful). There is no fast travel as well, so prepare for A LOT of walking, as you go back and forth to explore the same locations during the night and day. It's just... not fun. It's tedious. + when there is no ambient things going on AND when you kill everything there is to kill on your way somewhere, it gets even less fun and more tedious/boring.
The story has a very strong mysterious feel to it and the music that plays when you find temples that are connected to the story adds even more to that atmosphere. A bunch of collectibles like hats and skins and bed upgrades. Also some other collectibles that don't seem to do much, apart from makin your cave prettier/more lively. The combat is not good. The hit detection is shoddy. Character progression has some bad decisions to it, like mobs adding attributes rendering Bear Points (which could be used as experience so players could upgrade stats themselves) useless. Mobs/food doesn't respawn, making your world emptier as you progress. No fast travel. Expect to spend most of your time going back-and-forth to your cave to change from night to day or day to night, as some things happen at night or day.
I still recomend this game. It has lots of negatives, some positives, but I don't think those negatives are beacuse of the developer being terrible at... coding or something. Some locations actually look interesting and are well made. I think that he just made some bad decision here and there. Considering how this is his first game, it's not surprising that he made a few things wrong (like making Bear Points useless... I know, I can't get over that, but it just bothers me a lot, since they could work as experience points. Missed potential right here.), but hey, if you don't fall... you... won't know how to stand up? IDK, I'm not good at this.
Overall, it was a tedious/boring adventure so far. The only thing that kept me going was the mysterious thing/story in the game. If you can look past all the other things and focus on the story and mysteriousness/exploration you might put some hours into it... like me.
If you can't look past the problems... this is not for you.
Also, I'm not here to give life advice to the developer, beacuse he feels sad the game got so much hate. I feel sorry for him, I really do. But I'm here to review the game, something the developer can use to better his next game, or update the current one. That's it.

I don't know where to start with this but let's just try:
My first experience with ArmA was with the Operation Flashpoint Series and later on with ArmA 1 (Cold war Assault) and then ArmA 2 (+ all possible Add-Ons).
And i just have to say, that i freakin fell in love with this game (ArmA3) from the very begining.
Sure there were heaves of problems, bugs and♥♥♥♥♥♥going wrong at the beginning but i still bought this game as soon as it was availabe (Which should've been like early Alpha or so).
But to explain why i sank over propably 2000 hours of my life into this game:
-Versatility: With the workshop added and all the mod support the game offers, it's just incredible for how long you are able to find new stuff. New Maps, weapons, uniforms, AI-Units, vehicles, helicopers, tanks, etc. etc.
-Versitility: With the ZEUS Modul and the Ed3n Editor you are able to creato soooooo much stuff. You can create YOUR OWN scenarios, and the overview them and change them while playing with zeus. if you play with a few people and you keep changing the missio maker you never ever ever run out of ideas/scenarios to play.
-Versitilititititiy: I think we've bee here before... With the huge mod support theres other beefits aswell. If you are playing onlie you will be able to find all sorts of server. wether you like playing as a lone wolf and kill other players, play in a huge team vs. AI encampments/bases, or just get flipping rich with selling apples. there's something for everyone out there.
But i don't want to hail everythig into the sky here, so here's a few negatives, which imo you should kow before you buy this:
-This game is in NO regards something for people lookig for a run & gun game. It's a Mil Sim after all.
-With the milsim aspect comes the complication of finding key bindings for everything you want to be able to do. so be preapared to learn buttloads of them (Especially with TFAR and ace in play).
-The graphics may look BRILLIANT on a good rig but if you are on minimum specs prepare for some frame problems,
especially on bigger servers (although i have to say BI optimized a lot with the last few updates)
But other then that i can really just recommend this game if you are into military shooters that own you huge piles of different stuff.
And since my "N" key is ♥♥♥♥ed, here are some Ns for you guys that made it this far: n, n, n, n, n, n, n, n, n, n, n
That should've made up for the missed ones.

Diary Entry 1- Heliopolis is under siege by Rome. I've been unable to send reinforcements because Caeser is moving his troops around my territory, destroying farms, mines and villages. I can't spread too thin in fear of my other cities being attacked.
So 5 handfuls of Heavy machine Gunners have been defending the city from catapult bombardments and grenadier attacks.
And now, he seems to have set his sights upon the neighbouring city of Memphis.
Diary Entry 2 - I've reached out to the Malinese and Isabella of Spain, and both have declared war on Ceaser. They are on the opposite side of him to me. So while they cannot directly help my cities, they will put pressure on the Western side. So hopefully I can repel the siege and push to his cities. I have a troop of tanks coming in from the Northeast, and a regiment of Marines coming in from the southeast.
Diary Entry 3 - The marine regiment was ambushed on both sides upon coming around a mountain. Despite the enemy taking heavy losses, we lost the regiment.
Luckily a reinforcement squad was detailed to memphis, so now it's a case of bunkering down for the incoming attack, and planning the counter offensive.
The tanks have made significant progress, taking the city of Ardea from the grasp of the Romans. They will continue their progress north, towards Rome itself.
Diary Entry 4 - A reserve regiment of Marines have rendezvoused with the tanks. The dispatch will push on to Rome, flanking from the south, whilst Memphis defends and draws the brunt of the Roman Empire.
Diary Entry 5 - We took two cities to the south. And i decided it was now the time to counter attack. Making losses along the way, we broke through the memphis siege, and took the city of Ostia. It was short lived however, as the enemy retaliated while we were at our weakest and reclaimed the city. Luckily, the reserve squad was just 1 click behind, so now we can retake the city again, and await reinforcements.
I see very little action on the Western side, I am beginning to believe my allies have hidden motives. Their troops linger on the enemies borders. Perhaps waiting until I am weak enough that they may strike both me and Julius Ceaser. I must prepare for this eventuality.
Diary Entry 6 - I was wrong to doubt Isabella. How could I let the seeds of battle cloud my mind. She commenced her march across the border today, and in one fell swoop, she liberated a city from the enemy. Her troops have now joined mine, and we march together to the heartland of Mother Rome-ia
Diary Entry 7 -  Isabella and I, sat down today and signed the Permanent Alliance of our two peoples. We will forever be comrades in arms, and for this, I graciously gave her 3 cities as gifts. Not without proper thought mind you. They are in 3 strategic places to mine enemy and mine future enemies. This will allow us to adaquately aid each other in times of war, and even further each others growth.
To our future! -clinks glass-
Diary Entry 8 - Rome has fallen to Spain! I made a good choice in allies, Isabella is ruthless, a worthy opponent to any who may cross her.
The Chinese also declared war on Germany, Frederick reached to me.. unfortunately, as well as the war on the Romans is going, I cannot extend myself at this time. He seemed disappointed.
Diary Entry 9 - An achievement I am unsure of. We have created...The Atom Bomb. I don't know what to think about this. A weapon with destruction beyond any imagination. One that would win countless wars, but with such heavy costs. I must make sure this never falls into the hands of our enemies..
Diary Entry 10 - We were pushing the city of Cumae today, they had heavily fortified the city, and it seemed an arduous task. The combined might of myself and Spain, and yet we struggled.. A shadow appeared on the horizon. They came bearing the flag of Rome, and begun a charge on our flank. We were outnumbered, the rest of our forces had lagged behind to clear up the enemy remnants. We hastily mustered a defence as best we could. The doors to Cumae opened, the cities huge force came out to greet us. We were preparing for defeat..
But then there they came. The Malinese army! They routed the enemy on our flank. Taking advantage of this turn of tide, we charged the enemy city, gates wide open and with morale turned, we claimed it for our own.
Diary Entry 11 - It's been a long war, spanning many years. Due to the efforts of our 3 way alliance, we have chipped the Romans down to a fraction of the strength they once possesed. Brundisium is their final city, their last stain on a world so tainted by greed. I have the honour of being the one to remove that stain. I now make my march, our footsteps of doom bellowing down upon the city walls. We are coming..
Diary Entry 12 - As we approached the gates of the Palace, Ceaser panicked. He offered a Peace Treaty, along with all his coffers. "Why barter for what I can simply take?" I said, leaving a lifeless corpse on the floor. My troops rejoiced, sharing drinks with the Spanish, and food with the Malinese. What was I doing? I was looking across the border to the North... towards the prosperous Chinese Empire.
Honestly, you have to be a fan of these types of 4x games, to enjoy them. A lot of people find them boring because there's a decent amount of waiting around while you wait for buildings to finish, units to be trained, research to be finished etc. Saying that, I find Civ games to be faster paced than games such as Crusader Kings/Europa Unversalis. The learning curves are a lot smaller too!
You'll never find great graphics in these types of games, but you'll always find amazing gameplay, and that's what matters right? Great gameplay is what keeps you playing, not great graphics.
I'm not a fan of the newer games, Civilization: Beyond Earth especially. I think they completely ruined that game. However, if you enjoyed the previous games (1, 2, 3) or you want to get into the series without spending a lot of money. I whole heartedly recommend this game.

Whether you want to play it like an economic or diplomatic power, or play it like a 4x war-style game (like most people do), it's got something for everyone.  Lots of customization, expansions, and mods to keep it fresh. Everything from fantasy RPG style scenarios, to space ship battles, to my personal favorite - next war; featuring giant tanks and mechs.
Matches can be as short as a few hours or as long as a few weeks.  Great turned based strategy that blends the need to balance economy, science, and culture with military might or defense.

This game makes you feel like you're in the 90s, it sucks you into that world, and your train of thought start going all retro. Typical from Mario is to check if pipes are actually usable, here it's the walls you break. Some of them have marks on them, some do not. Anyways, to the point.
I started the game for the first time the other day, and I fell in love instantly; the graphics, the sounds, the attack of Shovel Knight, the enemies and jumps, everything was perfectly connected and pleasant, I thought "Man, this is one of those games that makes you want to play constantly!"
The fist 3 hours I had loads of fun, visiting villages, getting the roamers on the map, the random bosses, the hidden stuff, the upgrades. I simply loved it, and everytime I closed the game, I couldn't wait to boot it up again.
But then, the feeling-good gameplay stopped, and I found myself thinking "I really want to end this level, it's not enjoyable like the others, and hope the next one is less frustrating", alas, the next level never was more enjoyable, at contrary, it was harder and less fun to play.
Also want to mention that one thing that I don't like about the game, is how they try their best to make every level different, that means that you won't play the same style of level again; for example, there's one level that consists of winds pushing you around, and you being smart and using it to your favor, that was fun, but that mechanic only lasted 20 mins, once the level was done, you won't see the same background/music/enemies again, and it happens with *every* level.
I loved the first levels of the game, but they never appeared again, and that made me sad, because they were far more pleasant.
Another game mechanic that I don't think is done right, is the "night". Basically, it makes all the screen black and you don't see neither the character, the enemies, nor where you put your foot, unless there's a thunderstorm (one each 5 or 6 seconds that lasts for 0,5s) or a hole in the background which lets light pass through. It was frustrating to constantly die due to an enemy hitting you without you noticing, and falling to the depths; losing coins for something you have no control over.
So, basically, after the first 3 hours, I started not feeling good playing the game, it was death after death after death, and it didn't make me feel good like the way Dark Souls saga does after accomplishing something, sometimes I thought it was pure luck that I was still alive.
Game is short, some mechanics will make you pull your hair out, and you never get to enjoy the levels/mechanics/enemies that you love again. However, the gameplay is extremely fun, using the shovel is so entertaining and original/creative, that you just can't wait to see a pile to dig, or a normal enemy to use it, the sound is spectacular, and the graphics are pleasant to your eyes, it's one of those games that you want to watch at everything in the screen to notice the great details in it.
Up until hour 3; 8/10, after hour 3; 5/10.

To say "not recommended" isn't necessarily the vibe of what I want to give from this review. Ultimately my sentiments would lean more toward a neutral response, but "not recommended" captures my intention more than recommended does. I wouldn't recommend this game, not because it's a bad game, but because it's not a good game. It's mediocre. It may appeal to people who thought Zelda was too difficult, but that's about the extent that my recommendation goes.
Ultimately the biggest problem with the game is that it's way too easy. I played it on normal mode, so naturally I don't expect the monsters to be anything special, but that's not the kind of difficulty that I'm talking about. I mean that the puzzles are way too easy and the dungeons are way too linear. Perhaps I shouldn't compare it too much to Zelda, but that and God of War seem to be what most people compare it to. I can definitely see the inspiration of Zelda on the game, but they've dumbed that down into only a handful of dungeons that are extremely simple to navigate through and beat. There are a couple of decent puzzles that leave you with a sense of accomplishment, but once again comparing it to the quality of Zelda, it leaves something to be desired.
Most of these easy puzzles are accomplished by gimmick weapons that are found in the dungeon that you'll find yourself using it the most. Generally these weapons serve little practical purpose outside of the dungeon they're found, though there are a few exceptions. One such gimmick item is one that greatly resembles the gun from Portal. When I first saw it I thought "awesome, I can portal around everywhere now. What a great idea!" But unfortunately that excitement was stifled by the realization that you can only use the gun on a handful of orange circles. It was kind of cool going around with it, but they overused the gimmick in the dungeon to the point that it felt tedious, and they only used it a couple of times outside of the dungeon to get little secret items. The horse, Ruin, was also like this. The horse was cool when you could use him, but War is limited to using the horse in only certain areas. I had hoped that a game about a horseman would feature more horse, but the game is pretty close to the end by the time you even get him.
The power glove item that lets you smash the blue crystals was neat since you could use it as a weapon, but it really wasn't that great of a weapon either. For the most part I found myself only using the sword and the crossblade (the boomerang) in battles, and the latter was still pretty weak, but could help subdue certain enemies. I almost never used the wraith skills (though they may prove more helpful in Apocalyptic difficulty). The chaos form was pretty helpful, though perhaps it made the game too easy.
The story is one of the areas where the game does shine. I don't want to give too much away, but it is pretty unique, and perhaps it's the only thing I really liked about the game. The characters are decent and likeable too, though admittedly the names can be a little confusing at first. The swordplay isn't bad either, though it can be tedious at times. Maybe I had an issue with this because I never used my wrath items or other weapons, but the sword just worked better than the rest of them. Your character controls a lot like a character from World of Warcraft, which works pretty well. I only have two gripes with the movement. The first is that when you're targeted onto a character and you use your dash move, it moves your character relative to the screen rather than relative to your character. This leads to your character darting toward an attacking enemy rather than dashing to the side periodically. It would have been more intuitive if it had been done relative to the character. The second gripe is that the horseplay can be a little clunky as well, though this is a relatively small problem.
The game suffers from bugs as well. Perhaps this is more situational to the player, but during my runthrough of the game it crashed between five and ten times. It wasn't super bad, but it was highly annoying. Additionally, sometimes when you're climbing on that demonvine stuff and you want to jump to another piece, it won't let your character do it, and you have to try again. Similarly, often after you land one such jump your character will be stuck there unable to move. Another glitch I ran into is that often when you try to summon your horse, it will summon him for a second and then your character will immediately unsummon him, which can be pretty annoying. One final bug that I noticed was that sometimes the music would  partially cut out and the game would sound hollow. A restart fixes this, but it's still annoying. These bugs may just be limited to a few people, though, so I don't necessarily calculate them into my real recommendation, but they're worth noting.
Exploration felt pretty shallow. There were some neat areas to explore, like one area called the Drowning Pool, but for the most part there wasn't much to explore since the game is so linear. A lot of the exploration in the game relied on going back to old areas with new abilities, which was kind of tedious since it relied on backtracking rather than new challenges. It was kind of cool opening up old areas, but if you don't remember exactly where they were, then you have to go through the whole ordeal of the dungeon again, which proved to be banal, though the puzzles were precompleted by you. At least there was some sense of exploration, but as I said, what was there felt shallow.
The soundtrack to the game is fine too. Nothing to get too excited over, but not necessarily bad either. Just fine. And the game could have expanded more on a certain subplot featuring a certain dapper undead, too. At least it was there at all, but the game didn't really do anything with it. It could have been awesome, but it was just left there uncompleted.
All in all the game isn't necessarily a bad game, but there's nothing to make it good either. I was expecting more given all of the great reviews. I'd officially rate the game as average: okay, but nothing special. I wish Steam gave a "neutral" button when deciding how to rate the game, but "not recommended" is the better choice of the two recommended options. Cheers.

This game is basically a discount GTA SA, but it's still a lot of fun. If you can get it on sale for under $10 with the DLC it is worth it.
Some people report problems with this game and Windows 10. I've had no problems, other than a bit of lag when things get busy, and it sometimes opens in windowed mode, for no reason (runs fine full screen). There are some bugs in the game, like graphics glitches, peds & cars stuck in walls/floors, and places in the map where you can't get out (and need to reload to escape). Load times are also long, and sometimes you briefly get a black screen instead of the loading screen. But the game is old and slightly unpolished, so these things are expected.
The best part of the game is customizing your character and your cars. You can't customize DLC cars, though, or any non land vehicles. It greats riding around in a tricked out golf cart wearing nothing but lingerie, high heals and a punch perm. The cut scenes in the game are well done, though a lot of the humor is crude or just unfunny.
It's also very easy to get money in the game - no Shark Cards here! Just do some missions and buy some stores and then... leave the game running while you go do something else. You get money every in game hour, though you have to go to your phone to pick it up. By about level 25 or so you will have all the money you need. You can trade extra money for respect, which helps you level up.
Looking for collectables can be fun, but like in most games there are too many, and the payoff is generally low. The photo ops do give you about $1000 so early in the game they are good for money. Like GTA the game has stunt jumps - they are hard to find but fun to do. Unlike GTA, SR3 has shortcuts that once you find them, the GPS will use to get you places faster. Again it's hard to find them, though in this case it's more of trying to tell which of the many little back streets are shortcuts that the game recognizes. These little alleys are also sometimes not even worth taking, as in a fast car it might just be better to blast down a main road (in the wrong lane, of course) to get to your destination. There are also some off road shortcuts that the game doesn't tell you about but they save a lot of time.
The map is not huge, but it's still a decent size. Unlike GTA all of the map is accessible from the start of the game, but there are a lot of interior spaces that you can only use in missions, or that you need to do missions to unlock. You can go inside stores, cribs, some ships and a few other places, but most buildings can't be entered. A lot of the areas of the map look similar and its sometimes hard to tell where you are without going into the phone. There is also not a lot to do in the air or on top of buildings (other than barnstorming & collectables hunting), but there is virtually nothing to do in the water, outside of a few missions. You can swim, though, which is sometimes handy as a short cut, because you can warp from the water to the shore.
Pedestrians walk most on sidewalks and alleys, while gang members can appear in some other locations. There are no pedestrians/NPCs in the water, so you can only get boats in specific places. But that's OK, because boats are mostly useless, and the mapping system sometimes doesn't know how to get you to places in a boat. You can also only access planes from the airport or the crib you buy there (though you can get the Saints jet fighter at some other cribs). You can also generally only get helicopters/VTOL aircraft at cribs with helipads, but not at the airport one. You also can't get cars at the airport crib, even though it's on ground level. There are no NPC or AI flown planes or helicopters other than in missions and the ones that enemies bring out when you♥♥♥♥♥♥them off. There is also no trains, so CJ & Big Smoke have nothing to worry about here!
The missions are BS even compared to those in GTA- you have to drive to whoever is giving you the mission, and from there you usually have to drive to the actual start point. It's a lot of pointless driving, padding out the game length. Some missions are just cut scenes, or they are just introducing an activity. In many missions it's just you shooting at things while an NPC drives/flies. However, most are run & gun type activities, where you can't use anything but the weapon they give you (or your fist), and you have to take the path that is given. You sometimes have a brute thrown at you, and have nothing to fight it with (you need another brute or a BIG weapon to take those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s down). And when you leave/finish the mission (or die), you get sent to whatever crib is closest. You can't pick one like in GTA.
Sometimes when you start mission, you can bring the homies/followers you got before starting, but sometimes they get kicked out. Sometimes you can call someone in, and other times you can't all anybody, not even for a car. Often missions will give you an NPC to accompany you, but they often just get in your way or slow you down (as do your regular homies/followers). In one mission I had Shaundi fall off a stair case, refuse to get into the helicopter, and fall out of a window. That's three times for one mission that I had to reset because of the NPC. If I had been by myself I would have finished in one go.
Some of the activities and mini missions are fun. The best are the insurance fraud activities, but there is only a few of those. The professor Genki ones could have been their own game. The ones where you destroy things are fun as well, though some of the others like the Escort ones are just tedious. There are no mini games like in GTA, but there still endless calls from NPCs. They just want you to do mini missions instead of going bowling. The calls are particularly annoying because the button to answer a call is the same as to get in a car. It's also the same button to open a door, grab a human shield, go shopping, warp to shore, and access your crib. There is no way to change it, so you will often try to get into a car and end up answering the phone instead, or trying to leave your crib through the door, but accessing the crib menu instead. This is probably the most annoying thing in the game, along with the the constant reminders that you can do xxx through your phone, and the stupid quick time event style combat you sometimes are forced to use.

Just got I think as far as I could into the game, and I enjoyed every minute of it, MOSTLY, nearly completeing everything at 100%. Of course, it took its fair amount of patience, but I rarely lack in that field. That, AND, I'm a huge fan of exploration games, and that's mainly what this game is+adventure+some platforming, rather than a simulator.
You explore to find out what the goal of the game is and its story. To find out why you're playing as a bear. To find out the indications of what you need to do. To find out why you lack stats to eat certain foods or do certain things, even if it doesn't really make sense. And, if you give the game the chance to, it's really made well enough that you get your answers if you bother going beyond what you're maybe usually use to go in video games. Bear Simulator DARES not take you by the hand and show you the way, and instead, pushes you to get out of your comfort zone.
You're not given a map. So what? The game's environnement is designed well enough that you can make your own map in your head without getting confused. There's a whole bunch of beacons and landmarks everywhere, and nothing looks exactly the same. After playing about 10 hours, I knew my way around the entire game world pretty darn easily and if you can run it on high graphics, some of the environnements are pretty darn neat-looking, especially one region of the game, even WITH some low-res and stretched textures.
The game has also a good share of surprises and things that are, depending on how easily you can be amused, pretty worth working hard to unlock, especially after grinding your stats and unlocking new abilities.
Now, for the less positive. Yes, indeed, the game has its BIG share of bugs. Like, I got stuck in some parts of the environnement many MANY times and had to go back to the main menu to reload AND the hit detection is sometimes very ackward, even if you can get it working right after a while.
Yes, the game is rather unfinished, but if you can get pass those two aspects, which I think are the two major ones, to me, really, this was pretty darn worth the money I spent on it, and I would love to see it get properly finished with ALL the other remaining mysteries still left unanswered after completing the last possible objective.
So, overall. Yeah. It ain't a game for everybody to enjoy and you gotta like the gendra and be able to forgive silly things and some bugs here and there to be able to fully have fun playing it. And this, I got all that was needed to achieve.

I bought this game as it was recommended by Steam as being similar to Uplink and Hacknet. If that is why you are here, do not buy this game. It is nothing like either of them. In fact, I couldn't really recommend this game to anyone and am genuinely baffled by the number of positive reviews.
It is not fun or enjoyable at all.
It is a simulation of clicking on broken links, clicking randomly all over the websites that do load, resetting your router and looking out your window. There is no point in scouring each site for clues in the hopes of slowly unravelling a dark conspiracy. Just pure, mindless, brute-force clicking. The "hacking" tag is there because you will be randomly hacked if you go too long between router resets. The "hacking" minigames are awful, and, again, nothing like Uplink or Hacknet. In one, you click around some squares so they don't touch other squares; in another, you click arrows so they point towards other arrows; in the last, and worst one of the three, you must transcribe several case-sensitive lines of random code. If you have yet to buy the game and are wondering if this is fun or not, go to a random web page, right click it and go to "View Source" then type everything you see into Notepad. If you loved that experience but would prefer to first be laughed at by a pixellated skull, this may be the game for you.
So if it does not appeal to hacking game fans, it must appeal to horror game fans. Again, I am confused. Other than the frustration of being hacked after finally getting two pages to load successfully, the horror comes from two jump scares. These are both described in the tutorial and are utterly nonsensical. One is a maniac killer who won't kill you if you turn your lights off, the other is a kidnapper who won't kidnap you if you hold  your door handle. Once you have experienced both, they too become frustrations that you have to work around and you settle into a pattern. Click a link, click 'back' when the page doesn't load, click another link, click around randomly on that page, reset your router, click another link, click randomly some more, turn off your lights, check the front door, click another link, get hacked, rinse, repeat.
The biggest frustration comes from the fact that there feels like there is so much potential in this game. The dark net pages, when they do load, are genuinely disturbing, as is the overall premise of trying to find a link to the Red Room. But you don't get to savour the atmosphere as you are busy clicking around like a madman and plotting your next router reset. This review would not have been so negative if there had just been a way to read the websites at your own pace.
The game is cheap enough that writing this review might come across as a bit silly, but at time of writing, Hacknet is on sale for nearly the same price (and is still worth it even when it's at full price) and is an infinitely more fun game. Please, do yourself a favour and look at some Youtube playthroughs of this game before downloading it. But judging by its popularity, I wonder if Welcome to the Game is just some in-joke that I missed the punchline to.
While it is more fun than CS:GO with its other mechanics, its pay to win. You can pay to have the best armor, and weapons ffs, and their prices are way too high for the equipment.

Woah, well, that was short!
Looking over a few of the reviews, there's not a lot I can contribute to this.  I was expecting something like TakeOnMars, but what this is, seems to be a short demonstrator for, a generic 'mission'-based physics/maths tutorial for kids, themed around planetary exploration.
You're cast in the role of  "The Commander" of a two-man crew (but the other dude vanishes halfway through), and have to rescue an astronaut who's crashed on the other side of the hill by figuring out how to get there using some trigonometry... Except Trig's probably a bit too tricky, so all the game has you do is a few divisions on a calculator, and the game pretends to do the trig for you...
I can see where they were going with it, and I hope they can clean this up and add some more missions, but I have to say, I can't really recommend it to anyone:
The play length is ~5 minutes, if that.  All the assets are there: Models, texture maps, voices, a GUI, etc... But it's all rough and unfinished, and given where the pilot 'crashes', I felt I could probably just walk there, rather than go through all the rigmarole of triangulating positions.
No, I can't, in my heart, recommend this to anyone, I'm sorry.  If you want to play astronaut, play Space Engineers, or TakeOnMars.   This looks like a late-90s attempt at a 3d demo / maths tutorial.     If it was far more polished, and had a couple of missions, then perhaps I'd give it a thumbs-up, but nobody should really pay money for this, sorry :(

After pouring more than 500 hours into this game, I think I can safely say that I can write a good review of this game. For those who enjoyed action rpgs such as diablo and torchlight, you probabaly will enjoy this game. Sacred 2 is an open world hack n slash rpg that is filled with massive amounts of content. I have to say the thing that keeps me playing this game is the leveling. Leveling up in this game is so much fun and super addicting. Gameplay is pretty solid, although it could be better in my opinion. Loot is definitely an aspect where Sacred 2 shines. The feeling of satisfaction you get after picking up PILES of loot from slain enemies is amazing. The character classes are all really fun, each have their own unique playstyle and all classes (excluding the seraphim and inquisitor) can choose between a shadow campaign or a light campaign.
Now I did mention this game is similar to diablo; however, if you are looking for the same level of challenge as diablo II, then this game does not have it. So for those who like a really high challenge, you might want to try a different game. This game is also known to have many glitches, which is why many others playing this game suggest the community patch. Personally I have not used the community patch and I have not ran into and game-breaking glitches.

I have played a little of Estranged: Act II so far and I am impressed with the big improvements. The Unreal Engine really shows off many details. I recommend Estranged: Act II, but beware, this is an early access title, so bugs and glitches may occur(I have already seen some, got stuck behind a whiteboard and couldn't get out.)

I feel that Narcissu's story succeeds at its goal, which is to make the player, or reader, feel the protagonist's sadness and loneliness. However, Narcissu 1st attempts to do so through a bland male protagnist and a flat female protagonist, which makes the first game hard to finish. Bear Simulator instead focuses on is creating a setting where there is a story to be told that the player has to discover by exploring as much as they can and finding food and clues as to what's going on. Pros:
Interesting story - The character you play as (Daniel) lost his memory, but a note he left to himself describes that he has to kill this evil man at the very bottom of this castle, deep in the dungeons. Along the way, you collect more of Daniel's diary and uncover the reason behind why this man needs to be dealt with.
Creepy setting - The castle of Brennenburg is quite scary because the guy who owns this place is a horrible person and the story within this castle makes it all that much creepier. Some areas you come across make you not want to take another step forward because you know that there is some scary events that are about to go down in this area that you are about to progress through.
Scary monsters - These 'servants' are freaky as hell, especially because you can't fight them back. You have to hide in the darkness so that they do not see you.
Puzzles - I'd hate to admit it but I had to look up a few sections because I had no idea what to do. But there was one part where something you have to do to progress is so random that you would never guess unless you are some kind of strange genius.
Music - When servants see you and are headed your way, the music really adds fear to the situation, like a scary movie in theaters. The music really matches this abandoned castle, because it makes you feel like you are alone, but you know you are not alone.
Gameplay - Daniel loses his sanity the longer you are in the darkness...you need to reach lit areas to progress. You have to limit how many candles/torches you can light because you don't collect many tinderboxes. And if you light hallways, it could mean the death of you because if the servants see you and chase you down the hallway, they will still see you in this light and chase you all the way through. It is all made worse because you CANNOT FIGHT BACK!
Scariness - OK, this is the scariest game I've played, and I'll tell you why. The developers didn't rely on cheap jump scares. They put in pure scary content, the monsters ('servants') are scarier than all hell, you panic when you even hear one of these creatures. When you run out of lighting resources (tinderboxes and lantern oil), you panic. When you enter certain areas, you know you are going to encounter these things just by looking through the entrance.
Cons:
Voice Acting - The voice acting in this game is subpar. Yes I understand that this isn't an A-list game, but you can get some better voice acting in here.
Character Design - Every body except the servants in this game are complete♥♥♥♥♥♥ The living humans you come across in this game have horrible design. The dead humans you come across in this game have horrible design. I know this is a strange thing to point out, but the naked bodies in this game are made like♥♥♥♥♥♥ The male bodies' junk is just a cylindrical lump on the body. My point is, if you can't make a body part right, cover it up, especially if it is an unessiantial body part to look at, like a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
The Ending - I won't spoil anything but I'll throw spoiler tags on it anyway...
Verdict:
Even though this game has some issues, it is still a good game. You'll mainly enjoy it for the scares though, as the voices and graphics kill your vibe outside of the parts where you are running or hiding from the servants. This game is worth full price because it is only $20, and the amount of scary content you get in this game is worth it. It also has a decent replay value to it because you can get your friends to play this, and watch them spaz out while they play it. Recommended to anybody looking for some good scares.

I've only got about 3 hours in this game so far and I've got to say, I was terrified for about 2.5 of them. The aim of the game here is to find codes within sites on 'the dark web', solving puzzles and navigating fictional sites to string together a web address to reach the end game. When a code is found, it can be recorded in your notepad (in game). Once you've figured out what you need to do, the puzzle sections are fun and challenging and the hack mini games become more and more difficult as you progress. You have 30 days to find the URL and each time you're hacked you lose time and occasionally, your notes.
Sounds pretty straightforward right? Throw in the threat of kidnap and a mouth breathing serial killer and your task of finding several codes becomes slightly more ominous. The deeper you get on the 'dark web', the higher the threat of being tracked down and abducted becomes. I guarantee, every floor board creaking, voice in the shadows and threatening phone call will set your nerves on edge - forcing you to find a balance between situational awareness and puzzle solving which gets more difficult to manage the longer you play. Good luck, you'll need it.
Pro tip - watch the tutorial before playing for the first time if you want to have any idea what you're doing.

This program presents itself as a game, and to be honest, it fits the definition, but it's definately not something you'd expect to see on Steam. It isn't terrible per se, but it can do with a LOT of improvement.
For starters, the player moves around like a steady-cam; Everything is smoothed out, from the movement over hills down to the motion of the mouse. It feels unnatural to the point it seems you're playing a drone of sorts.
Then there is the geometery; Terrain smoothing has been around for about a decade now, and it could have been used to some extent and look better than it does right now. Even with graphics set to the max I can see the edges a mile away. It is sloppy and it shouldn't have to be that way. And this doesn't go for just the terrain. The objects, entities and vehicles themselves look bad because of this. It is impossible to make a curved geometery that works on all hardware, but there are shaders and filters and all sorts of tricks that are very effective on that front.
Texture quality; Well, there is some, just not a whole lot. This is again one of those points that would have been acceptable a decade ago. With an option 'Beautiful' I expect to see high resolution textures.
This would all be acceptable in a simulator, which I suppose this falls under, if the actual simulation demanded high detail or amount of calculations that would justify sacrificing graphical fidelity. And that is probably what upsets me the most; It looks and feels quickly assembled in a Unity editor with little to no attention to detail or features.
It looks and feels like a demo, which, at the time I bought it (a few years ago) was a bit more expensive than the 5 bucks (if not less) that's advertised these days.
It does a good job as an educational tool, however, for both children who want to be astronauts and game developers alike (the latter probably isn't a complement though). It has some nice lessons in frequencies and stuff, but that's about the only thing it has going for it. Wel...it has the NASA logo up front, and it pained me to see the Gates Foundation in there as well, especially since it has the tendancy to crash when ALT+TABbing, but that may just be me.
All in all I cannot recommend this for what it is. I love the idea, but there is no game here. What little simulation it has is completely on rails and there is no way to mess up or discover something that deviates from the main story, which plot also escapes me...
I hope some developers got a lot of experience out of this, and I'm not sure about it's current price, but if you see this for anything over 50 cents, just leave it be.
One final sidenote, this is an alpha test for Starlite: Astronaut Academy, to be released in 2014. That was a year ago. It has been sold (and still is) as seperate full-release title (There is no Steam Early Access disclaimer on the store page). These 2 things don't bother me as much as the fact that over the years there have been no updates, improvements or anything that indicates this being a work in progress or part of a bigger project which is still in progress (although I'm pretty sure that one's dead as well).

NOTE: This is not a joke review. This is my personal opinion.
Tactical Intervention is a little shooter that I like to call, "Flawed, but fun." As many of you (Or a small amount of you, I don't know) know, Tactical Intervention is a game brought to us by members of the team that created Counter-Strike, one of the best-selling games on the Steam marketplace. I originally installed this so I could experience basically a free-to-play Counter-Strike, since I didn't (and still don't) have the mony to buy CS:GO or any of the other games. And you know what? For me, this became less of a Free-to-play Counter-Strike to me. It started feeling like an entirely different game, with more features, but also more bugs, but those are expected from games that are free-to-play. I started off in mission mode, and the mission was, "Escort the VIP." I happily did so, and managed to get him so close to victory. After so many CTs lost and Ts killed, I was shot point-blank with a shotgun. But the vip was still alive, and the Ts were being pushed back by the CTs, and we eventually won, earning me, "First match." Okay, enough about nostalgic experiences, let's get to the pros and cons.First, the pros. 1: It's free. 2: It's realistic (Besides bugs). 3: There's a lot more features. Now the cons. 1: You need to spend a lot of ingame coins to buy something permanently. 2: It's buggy. 3: There's a high chance you'll get killed by a P2P player. Now, the bugs you can get past, as well as being killed by P2P players, that was their desiscion, but having to spend so much ingame currency for a new weapon is frustrating. Another story that I want to tell about this game is this: We were CTs, and we were supposed to fight the Ts back so they couldn't arm the bomb. I followed someone with a dog and assisted him, until he was killed. I shot the guy that killed him, and took the dog with me, and, I know a lot of people do this with other games, immediately bonded with it. Anyone Ts that tried arming the bomb we would kill, until they managed to plant the bomb at point b. Me and my dog pal ran as fast as we could, going through multiple Ts, and eventually making it to the bomb, disarming it just in time. I know this review is going to cause a lot of people to vote this negatively, since pretty much everyone who made a positive review on this game were joking, but I don't care. I love this game, even with the glitches and the high prices of weapons. I'm not saying you NEED to get this game, I'm just sharing my experience with this game.

玩了那么多新游戏，始终都不会抛弃它——Sacred2
虽说我是在2010年接触S2，但是我还没玩遍所有角色以及所有玩法呢。
1、六翼天使
主流玩法有双刀、大炮，主修第一系，以第三系作为辅助；也可以玩三系全修，以第二系为主，第一和三为辅助，这种玩法，可以使用第二系的魔法，也可以使用第三系的大炮，群怪用第二系的光柱、怼BOSS用第三系的大炮，配合第二系套装的百分比吸血，相当给力，当然这种输出没有纯大炮那么变态。具体攻略，可以到百度贴吧——神圣纪事的精品贴翻阅我的攻略。不管怎么玩，一定要记住六翼天使的2个神技：第一系的冲劲十足和第三系的神力防护。
2、高等精灵
主流玩法有冰电双修或者火电双修，高精妹妹是比较传统的法师，实力很强大。她的必学神技有电系的“强劲鼓舞”，是个很给力的BUFF，以及“驱散”。
3、龙法师
主流玩法有吹风流加炸弹人，两者组合，不管怼BOSS还是群怪，效率都是杠杠的。当然它还有辅助神技，在此就不再赘述。第一系的变龙，高难度没前途，弃之吧。
4、森林女神
俗称大妈，远程专家，第一系是精髓，主力输出战技，吹管简直逆天的存在，没有弓箭类的弹道，只要命中高，子弹秒到，拿着吹管施放多重攻击的那个CA，简直就像在用喷子，玩第一的大妈，装备就选第一系专用的套装，全凑齐以后出百分比吸血，铌金难度百分比吸血高达4%，相当恐怖，也算是弥补了弓箭和吹筒没有百分比吸血属性的遗憾，当然也可以用飞镖，一些飞镖带有百分比吸血属性，带上盾，闯铌金难度更安全。第三系树皮buff虽然丑，但是也是必学的，作为辅助，增加大妈生存能力。大妈还有一种玩法，就是双持，虽然效率没有使用远程武器高，但也值得一试哦。
5、神庙守卫
这个角色，上手比较难，推荐玩法，第一、三系同时修，如果偏重升级，先修第三系，源泉魔法中的冰火换着用，群怪效率杠杠的，特别是多倍怪MOD，经验值duang~~~，令你爽翻天，但是高等级单挑BOSS，恐怕就是第三系的弱点了，基本上没输出，这时第一系就派上用场了，用百分比吸血的武器去正面肛BOSS吧，第一系的护盾BUFF和战斗警觉都是神技，必须要学，在专注未精通前，战斗警觉最后一个进阶先留着，别转成BUFF，怼BOSS专用，开没开启，完全两个样，开了命中很牛，没开就是渣。详细攻略，可到神圣纪事百度贴吧精品贴翻阅。

It would be cool if at least it showed an animation of you running out of the car trying to get away before you get killed if not letting us do it ourselves in a chance to get another car. Other than that its a fun little game.

Escape: Close Call
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
You have one eye on the road and your other eye is looking frantically in the mirror while your ears are constantly overpowered by the sirens of the police cars that are following you. The only thought in your mind is “Only 10 minutes, I just need to keep them at bay for 10 minutes to escape!” It is definitely going to be a close call!
Escape: Close Call is a frantic top down car game where you have to avoid being hit by police and other authority’s vehicles for ten minutes using all your driving skills, especially skids. Before you jump into your first game, I would strongly advise you to go through the twelve tutorial lessons.

Now that you are somewhat familiar with the controls and how to score the perfect combos, it’s time for you to try to escape this mayhem of police cars. The gameplay is fairly simple but extremely addictive. You will be awarded points when you avoid a car by a hair’s breadth; evade several cars within a short period of time to create a combo which will multiply your points. If you manage to get the authority’s cars to collide, they will explode and then one of two things will happen - either you run into them within a few seconds, in which case you will receive points and it will be part of your combo, or, if you did not run into them, a zombie policeman will appear and you will be able to run him over for additional points. However, when you do hit them, the screen will look fuzzy for a little while and it will become tricky to avoid the new waves of upcoming cars. Ten minutes is an eternity in the game. Put it this way, after 6 hours of gameplay I only managed to survive two and a half minutes at a time.  With the points you collect, you can purchase power-ups such as the gun turret which will help you to clear some cars coming onto your path for a short period of time or the gas tank upgrade which will give you more fuel. Oh, I forgot to mention that you have to make sure your gas tank is always as full as possible or you will lose by running out of petrol.  Just run over the zombies and you will be fine. Another aspect of the game that I really enjoy is the tasks you have to achieve to gain a new level of difficulty. The tasks will appear very quickly at the start of each run.
There are 25 cars to unlock, including a limousine! (a limousine . . ? How on earth you are going to survive 10 minutes with that one?)
I like the retro graphics in this game and the slow motion when you narrowly avoid cars or when you get caught out. The controls are good and responsive and you can play either with a gamepad or your keyboard.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Fun and addictive gameplay
-	Good retro graphics
-	Power-ups and upgrades to help you to survive 10 minutes
-	25 cars to unlock
-	Great price point
-	Achievements and trading cards
Negative:
~~~~~~~
-	Can be frustrating at times, especially when you die within a few seconds, several times in a row.
Escape: Close call is surprisingly good fun! A must-have!

A 20-minute look into the bleak future of United States space exploration if we continue cutting NASA's budget and failing to educate our citizens in math and science compared to other countries. The result is a game with physics that are all wrong and only 20 minutes of plodding, unrealistic content—all they could manage to create under these conditions before giving up. A real eye-opener, and a future none of us want to live in.

I enjoyed this. I backed it on Kickstarter and I don't regret that for a moment. It's a silly little collect-a-thon that reminds me of shareware games from yonks ago, along with a little bit of Twilight Princess's wolf Link, and a dash of walking simulator thrown in. It's a laugh being a bear. And honestly, some of it's pretty clever and I'd love to see the idea developed even further. It has some real potential behind it!
I've mostly played this in its Kickstarter Humble Bundle preview release version, and recently (finally) got around to switching to the Steam version. So I don't have too many hours here, yet.

After all the misogynistic, homophobic, racist, and generally unpleasant and imbecilic things that come out of his channel, it's really not clever to put any stock in it. He's discredited himself on countless, countless occasions. And the fans are often rabid and crazy enough to deserve being institutionalised. Not a good crowd.
So, that said, do I recommend this? Do you enjoy game where you've played as an animal or animal-like creature? Such as Okami, Ori, Twilight Princess, and so on? Do you like mysteries and collect-a-thons? Do you, perhaps, have an urge to eat all of the things? And do you enjoy playing games which are just a little bit different?
Then yeah. Be a bear. It's a laugh, and the price is right for it.

From developer stage-nana and publishers Sekai Project comes Narcissu 1st & 2nd, the story of a girl who has to choose between 7F and home.
This story focuses heavily on disease and suffering, of a girl having to medicate and go through the adverse affects of medication, and going through her life knowing that she will ultimately die.
I wasn’t sure what I expected when I downloaded this novel from Steam, and I went into it very confused at first. I just knew it was rated very positively, but it sat in my Steam library for a long time after downloading it. Finally, today, after realising I really need to clean some games out of my library to make room on my laptop, I decided to finally open this and play it.
What I definitely did not expect was to be moved to tears by a story such as this. It was incredibly moving, and the story really hit me in a lot of places I didn’t know I could be hit emotionally. The artwork in this really helps to move the story along, and the soundtrack as well, is just so beautiful, it really helps move the story along, and emit feelings in the reader that honestly made me have goosebumps. I have honestly, never been moved so much by just a simple visual novel – this affected me on the same level an incredibly sat film would.
Stage-nana did incredibly well with this story, and I would love to see more from this, and them.

This game is post Demonic-Armageddon 3D Zelda, full stop.
You play as War, one of the Four Horseman of the Apocalypse. This is not an incarnation OF the concept of war, who causes it by simply existing, or an immortal being invincible in combat, but a precusor to angels and demons who has gained enhanced powers that allow him to essentially play the role. Don't be fooled, you are renowned as a near-unstoppable force and not to be casually trifled with. The four horseman work for the Charred Council, an ancient institution designed to preserve the balance between Heaven, Hell, and Eath until mankind is ready to battle both and move into a new era.
You arrive on earth just as this conflict is beginning, but something is wrong. Your brethren, the other three horseman, are not present, and humanity is completely unable to defend itself. You quickly find your powers dminishing as your fight through demon and angel to find the source of the conflict, only to utimately be defeated by the demonic leader. You awaken before the charred council years later, accused of starting the conflict aahead of schedule and assiting Hell in emerging victorious. War protests this, and is given the chance to return to a ruined Earth to find and kill those truly responsible.
Gameplay is third person-combat and exploration, extremely similar to the Legend of Zelda series. You traverse zones of the ruined city that is the location of the game, but the zones are diverse and unique looking, from simple collapsed streets, to submerged subway tunnels, a worn cathedral and even an area transformed into a massive desert. Some areas are sealed or blocked on your first pass through, requiring a piece of equipment or new power you find by progressing in the story or locating in a dungeon.
War weilds the Chaos Eater sword, and can buy and find other secondary weapons along the way. Though War himself does not level up, the weapons do grow in strength as you battle with them. You can attach enhancements to the weapons that create multiple effects, from life-steal to better environmental damage to finding more currency in the world. While each weapon has a few starting basic moves and combos, you can purchase more from a merchant available in nearly every area using souls, the game's currency. Beating on an enemy enough can give War the opportunity to use a finisher, which invariabley end with a limb amputated or the enemy torn in half by an overwhelming, unstoppable attack. A dunegon into the game, you regain War's ability to pretty much become an avatar of war, unleashing his full power to become a monstrous flaming entity with insane damage and rediculous defense for a short time.
War himself has a health meter, which can be extended by beating a dunegon boss (sound familiar?) or finding four pieces of Life Stones scattered the world. War also has access to a few magical abilities powered by Wrath, aka mana. You can increase your Wrath by finding wrath shards in the world to create a new full bar in the meter, Later in the game you can begin to find pieces for an enhanced set of armor that skyrockets your defense when completed. Thus, combat itself does not level up War and increase HP or strength like a standard RPG, it is the equipment he finds that enables War to improve himself.
Equipment includes a boomerang like cross-shuriken that can be manually aimed or targeted at numerous foes, a pistol that allows for ranged combat, your trusty horse Ruin that can be summoned and dispelled at will anywhere it is available, a chain that allows War to grappel enemies or specific points in the world, and more.
So truly, nothing is completely original in this game; practically every piece of equipment or gameplay idea is derived from something else. But the game is fun regardless (or perhaps because of that). Enemies will gang up on you and attack together, later foes really put you to the test, bosses shift between figuring out patterns and exploiting a weakpoint using equipment or a straight up dash it, attack, and dash out/ block to avoid retaliation. The music is orchestral, with dark, ominous exploration themes to match a hellish earth and frantic, powerful battle themes for the bosses. The dungeons are well put together, and the game has far fewer moments of -look at this, go here, and do this- to solve the puzzles than modern 3D Zeldas do.
Some of the story is a little hard to grasp at first, simply because of the presentation, cutsences, and allusions to places or names you don't understand immediately, but it all can be figured out with time. The game is definitely violent, with War giving his foes no quarter and tearing them apart, spilling gallons of blood, and the demons love to roar in your face and seem all gritty and hardcore. If you can tolerate this, or enjoy it, and you appreciate the Zelda style of gameplay, get Darksiders.

This game has a lot of really good ideas, and most of them work as intended. I found it to be rather scary, although some times not for the reason that might have been intended. Wandering a dark hallway, trying to find the item you need to solve a puzzle or to advance, might sound simple enough, but the fact that the darkness is your enemy, as well the Servants, really makes you  have to think about what is the better idea. You can either run the risk of an enemy seeing you, or you can wander in the darkness and let your sanity drop, which may also lead to your death. It can be a hard choice at times, and you won't always make the right decision, but luckily there are enough checkpoints that you won't lose much progress if you lose all your sanity or health. The Servants themselves are freaky up close, although if you are seeing them up close, you are probably going to die anyway. And the fact that even looking at them drops your character's sanity means you mostly have to rely on hearing them, which is absolutely terrifying.
But of course, not everything works in this game. The puzzles are sometimes really tricky, as the game does next to nothing at times to give you a hint as to what you are supposed to be looking for, or what can be used on what and when. It usually is not a problem, but at times you might end up scratching your head, looking at your objective and inventory, trying to figure out how the items you have will get you to your objective. I had it happen a few times, but never enough that I got stuck for hours on end. Also, having health and health items on this game feels useless since you'll usually die in a hit or two anyway, so there really does not seem to be much point in having it. The biggest problem I found with the game is when it comes to escaping enemies. If I am spotted, even if I run and hide in the darkness three rooms away from where I was spotted, the Servants still seemed to be able to find me every time. They are faster than the character, so running can be hard if you are spotted and you're not near a doorway to run in to. I only ever managed to get away from any enemy once: I was killed every other time. Maybe I was just doing something wrong, but it was annoying nonetheless. Still, it only becomes a problem if you get spotted, so just be careful and it will never come up.

Amnesia: The Dark Descent is the holy grail of horror. The immersive plot, haunting atmospere, terrifying ambiance, and unearthly enemies make Amnesia the globally known horror game it is. From Mr. TotalPenguin to Pewdiepie, Amnesia has been a solid (and often hilarious) foundation for YouTube letsplayers since its release. Though most of its players don't scream and hyperventilate into a camera during the game, all of them experience fear, tension, and (occasionally) relief at reaching that save point. While I will agree that Amnesia plays on that old cliché, "Old mansion, crumbling hallways, grimy tables with rotting food, and massive "earthquakes" that last for 4 seconds and oddly don't damage anything", it is still a game that will startle, scare, and intrigue you to the very end. Even if you aren't a major horror fan, you should still try to play the game. It might suprise you how much you enjoy it!

Neutral:
- I generally didn't care about the Ninja escapades - because the stories and characters involved don't appeal to me.
Other Improvements:
- Only Team 7 and female characters seem to get fanservice dlc costumes......I really want to see new Kiba costumes (for example)
Overall I would rate the game a 4.5/10....If you've played the previous installments, I wouldn't recommend getting this. But If this is your first storm game then it would be more intriguing for our first play
