I've got a bit of a love hate relationship wth this game. I'm a huge fan of the Assassin's Creed franchise, but found myself frustrated with the mechanics of this game on a regular basis. It is in many ways an improvement on ACII, the addition of assassin recruits that you can call to assist when fighting is awesome. The story is also solid, both animus and Desmond arcs, even if there aren't many targets for Ezio to kill (outside of the optional side quests). And the addition of parachutes is great as you don't nhave to worry about falling to your death when you accidently fall from the top of the Colloseum.
However there in lies one of many things that are a niggle aboput this game. The movement is a back step from ACII. Oftenwhen trying to free run Ezio will either jump in the wrong direction, miss a leap of faith or sometimes just stop entirely and star hopping up and down on the spot. Add to this the you will often find that your weapon has been dissarmed and replaced with fists and in one of the Leonardo warmachine levels your vechicle stops responding to your input and this game becomes as frustrating as it is satisfying.
I'm still going to reccomend this game as there are so many more games out there that are worse than Assassin's Creed Brotherhood, which is full of redeeming qualities. That said I would advise against paying full price and look to get it when it's on sale.

I'm going to recommend this game with reservations.
Overall the presentation is good and if you like freecell then it is worth buying. The variation in the number of suits and stacks, as well as being able to develop more free slots throughout the game,  alters the difficulty and keeps things interesting.
I'm not sure that the rpg elements, overlaid on it, work all that well.   It is an interesting idea but I think it needs to be refined.  Freecell is a game that rewards taking time to think through numerous moves in advance.   The game, by having attacks upon your health while playing, which essentially functions as a fancy timer,   forces you to play quickly and make dumb mistakes as well as constantly interrupts your concentration.  The early boards are so simple that this isn't a problem, but as the game progresses you will feel more harried.  It becomes more irritating than enjoyable.  At one point, I found myself having to backtrack to capital cities to rest and restore my health and mana after one or two boards.  This was more a chore than anything else.   Thankfully this was ultimately alleviated by being able to open up another free slot.
Still, if you like playing freecell, this is a variation that I would try, especially when it's on sale.

Pretty good.  More hectic than I'd like.  You have to clear the board quickly because you will get attacked every so often.  I'm used to taking my time with puzzle games and I find it hard to think fast in this one.  But there are spells that help and armor you can buy to boost your defense.  You can heal at an inn, though they are few and far between.  There are one-time use only spells and also ones that you can learn in your spell book and keep permanently.  You can only have 10 active spells or items (one-time use scrolls) at a time, so choose wisely.
I have to say, though, that the map is epic sized.  Looks like an RPG or historical war game.  The graphics are nice for a puzzle game.  There is a little character that moves around on the map, but you don't see any enemies, it just goes to the puzzle screen.  And no story scenes or anything like that.  But there's enough to just spice up the usual freecell game and make it a bit more special.
The levels start out really short and easy but they do get harder.  Also you only have one free cell in the beginning.  You gain more by collecting random cards after winning battles or buying them from stores.  Once you have a full deck of all suits it lets you get another free cell, then you start again collecting for your next one.  Later levels have more than one set of card suits, like there might be on heart, one spade, but two diamonds and two clubs.  If you hover your mouse over a town it tells you the difficulty you are facing so you can decide where you want to go and work your way up to the difficult ones.  If you get into trouble you can back out, go heal, and come back to try again.  I haven't figured out if the levels are random or pre-arranged.  If they are random, then some of the difficulty is due to luck of the draw.

Shovel Knight is a amazing 8-bit platformer that takes major inspiration from other classic titles of the same genre like Castlevania,Megaman 2,Ducktales and Super Mario Bros but rather then just coming off as just an omosh to the classics of the 80s the game takes many of the tropes and cliches of those types of typical platform games and does something new with them. Disclaimer: I was one of the programmers on this game. But I did not design it, and this is my honest opinion.
If you enjoy FreeCell or other solitaire games, then definitely check out this game. It takes the standard game and adds a lot of variety to it. There's an element of limited time, since you're getting attacked, but you can also dispel the attacks before they are executed, giving you more than just the card sorting to think about. The difficulty gets harder than any other FreeCell I've seen, but you get spells to help you cope with that. Using the spells to "cheat" the rules of basic FreeCell is a cool twist.
The map artwork is beautiful, and freeing the cities as you go through the different nations is a fun way to track your progress. And there are a lot of levels, so you can play one file for a long time.
So in the end, it's FreeCell with added RPG mechanics. If that sounds cool, then this is for you!

Counter-Strike: Global Offensive is a lobby-based tactical shooter developed by Valve Corporation. Players join either the Terrorist or Counter-Terrorist team and complete objectives to win the match. CS:GO’s most well-known game mode sees Counter-Terrorists fighting to stop Terrorists from planting a bomb at a designated sight by eliminating them or defusing the explosive. At the start of each round, players purchase weapons using money earned from previous rounds. CS:GO’s community has developed an abundance of custom maps and game modes that expand or reinvent default gameplay. A huge assortment of in-game weapon cosmetics can be acquired by playing the game to distinguish yourself from other players.

To start it off, i'm a big fan of dc cinematic universe, and the year 2016, hadn't been a good year for me and the other fans. Even though, i'll state myself optimistic, since actually, all my hopes and expectation fall into this movie instead.
OK, Let's start with the strong aspects of the movie; performances and characters. well, i actually think this is what the director want to top off and show to the audience, thus forgetting the plot, which we will get into later. but the characters and the performances are well-performed- Margot Robbie as Harley Quinn really tops off my expectation. i'm a fan of harley quinn character, and she actually brought me the harley quinn i'm expected for- sexy, beautiful, it girl of joker's. while watching the movie, and whenever i'm feeling bored, harley quinn is there to make the scene fresh. and i think all audience, including audiences who didn't know her will love her and feel sympathetic to her. Will smith as deadshot actually didn't deserve much of my appreciation. i mean even though he's one of the great and strong aspect in the movie, i just thought i don't see will smith even trying to act, which weirdly works. watching Will smith here is just watching him using a kickass suit. Jared Leto as The Joker, is actually isn't the worst part of the movie (unlike what people might have said) i think that Jared Leto pull of a great effort into his character, and some scene of him showing up gave me goosebumps and own joys. but, maybe how little the scene for him is, or his character is pretty under-developed that just doesn't fit the puzzle in the movie. Viola Davis as Amanda Waller also brought up my her characther pretty well, as she played the cold-hearted leader Amanda Waller. other performances are great, like Joel Kinnaman, Jai Courtney, Jay Hernandez, Karen Fukuhara, and Cara Delevigne.
The chemistry between the characters are great, as well as the development between their relationship. in my opinion, one of the strongest chemistry is Harley Quinn and Deadshot. Their chemistry is electric, funny, and watching them teasing, and slowly started to care about each other, is entertaining, and make me ship them together. even, i have a relationship that had a weak chemistry, that is Rick Flagg and June Moore's relationship which is bland, forced, and unnecessary.
Now, parts that i think is the weak part of the movie, I think the plot is the main reason. The plot is lazy-written and under-developed,and at some point is pretty ridiculous. i don't want to get into it too much, since it will spoil some things, and i need you to watch the movie without spoilers, yet. even, i could tell you that the CGI is pretty cringy and sometimes, so does the visual effect between the scenes. the ending is actually rushed, predictable, and i think they could do better after building up the story of the fight scene.
At the end, everything has its bad and has its good, what i really suggest for you to do is just lower your expectation, yet don't miss it either. it may not lift the hype as in the greatness in the trailer, but i think it's still a great fun must see summer movie , and you should enjoy it without all the overly negative critics.

Where to start....
I had played the first game a while ago, back when steam wasn't famous and the visual novel genre wasn't really famous, it was my second Visual Novel ever, Tsukihime being the first.
I replayed Tsukihime not so long ago and with a greater capability for analysis I found it even more enjoyable and noticed some stuff I didn't notice the first time. Not so long ago I told myself "Hey, why not? Narcissu is now available on steam, let's replay it."
Just as with Tsukihime, I enjoyed it even more this time, and it was way more painful. They present a sad reality and execute it really well, the inner conflicts of someone who knows they will die soon without a specified date. The OST just fits perfectly for each scene and makes you feel even closer to the character during their conversations, even cheerful conversations can feel painful at times because of the tone the characters speak with(The VAs do a pretty great job with this, I was amazed). You notice the pain they are carrying inside and you feel for them.
And then comes side 2nd, which expands into this topic by presenting you another part of the conflict: Those who are left behind. The trouble close relatives go through when someone they hold dear  is close to dying, and how they try their hardest to support them despite their pain. And not  only that, but they develop further the main character from the first game and it makes you realize how she turned out that way. Every little detail mattered in the development of her character.
In the end, just like first, you go through a feelings roller coaster, the conversations tug heavily at your heart and the more you advance the more you know about the 7th floor and its patients. Each of the characters feel real and each of their interactions contribute to character development for every of them (This applies for both games).
It's truly an amazing piece of work. Soundtrack, writing, conversations, voice acting, characters. Sure, the art may not be the most appealing, but the feel you get from it is just right.

DEAD REALM - Review.
Dead Realm is Horror Hide & Seek in a nutshell. You start off either being the ghost/monster or you can be up to 8 players trying to hide from the monster until the time runs down. Naturally this would seem like a copycat to many mods on Gmod that allow a hide and seek type scenario but this is a bit different. In Dead Realm you are faced with strategic abilities that may make or break your chances at survival or dominance in the case of the ghost.
There are two game modes.
- Seek & Reap
- Bounty
Seek and Reap is basically your basic game of hide & seek, you have a set time limit you have to achieve in order to win whilst being granted 5 special abilities, You can clone yourself 2 times as a human, and use your shield up to 3 times. You can also take full advantage by using a camera monitor system similar to FNAF's. There is a meter in the far right corner that drains battery as you use your camera feature however so only use it in dire situations.
As the monster you have the ability to go invisible for a shirt period of time as it drains your stamina bar, you can also see through walls and find red heat signatures that show human players nearby or far away. If a ghost reaps a player, that player becomes an enemy ghost and will be able to reap other players.
Bounty mode - Bounty is a bit different where it's a basic game of Find the clues, escape whilst also being chased by a bloodthirsty ghost. In this mode, the players are tasked finding pocket watches left by the millionaire " Mr. Huxley " who according to the lore of the game murdered his wife and child and was either overtaken by darkness or left his mansion. You are tasked to find 10 watches left by Huxley all while avoiding reaping from the ghosts of his manor. (1 ghost) in the end of the game you are to run to a portal to escape the mansion, all while still being hunted. The ghost can see you but he has lower stamina and he cannot turn the souls he reaps into evil ghosts either.
Multiplayer - The multiplayer gaming system is peer to peer which always means, the people with the better internet reign supreme. This is bad because it causes major desynchs at times and major errors such as " YOU ARE BANNED " which has happened to me quite a lot.
PROS -
-  Unique atmospheric multiplayer horror game
- Fun with friends
- Creative mechanics
- New horror concept (Kind-of)
- Music is similar to a mix of Skyrim & Dead Island.
- Good User Interface
- Places to hide, unique locations
- CONS
- Peer to Peer Multiplayer gaming
- Limit of monsters and locations
- Two game modes (Both fun however)
- Basic multiplayer jump scare type game (Unique but could be darker and more ominous)
REPLAY VALUE - 8.4/10 - I'd play this only with friends or if I want to stream or record, or if I'm feeling a bit bored.
FINAL VERDICT - 7.9/10 - VERY GOOD
It's not often I say this about horror games since this technically isn't a horror game it's simply a multiplayer hide & seek horror aspect put into it. I will say this is a good game with loads of potential and I'm hoping the developers consider the possibilities in the near future and listen to some of the fan suggestions.
I recommend getting this game if you'd like to scare or get scared by your friends.

I rate the game Saints Row: The Third (AKA Saints Row 3) 4/5. Good.
This Grand Theft Auto styled, open-world, third-person perspective adventure game surpasses its predecessors in most respects. It's fun to play, works extremely well, has good graphics, an interesting, entertaining plot and is full of absurd humor while possessing very few drawbacks.
Perhaps its worst drawback though is its lack of true replayability. This game lacks any significant reason to ever replay it a second time as the choices you make in this game's open world have little effect on the plot. There is a single choice toward the end of the game that determines which of two endings you end up with and the game helpfully gives you the option of simply replaying that mission to see what would have happened had you made the other choice.
+Good graphics using an okay color palette though the game's colors look even more realistic when it's night time or rainy in the game world. The pop-in of graphics and textures are much less noticeable in this game than in most other Grand Theft Auto styled open world games. Of all the games of this general style I have ever played, only Just Cause 2 has better graphics. The city of Steelport of Saints Row 3 seems a little smaller than the city of Stillwater in Saints Row 2 but it is not terribly noticeable either. Characters and their clothes look pretty good also.
+Fantastic controls. Controlling helicopters and airplanes is easy and fun this time around. Cars handle well and your character is incredibly responsive also. The only bad thing about the controls was how the tanks handled. I should be able to turn the turret in any direction while moving in any direction without the turret's aim affecting the direction in which I am moving (that's supposed to be one of the main benefits of tracked military vehicles afterall). Refer to the free game Gear Up for how a non-walking tank with a turret should ideally handle in any game.
+Good though somewhat bland sound but good voice acting throughout.
+As in Saints Row 2, the character you created while wearing whatever clothes and jewelry you chose shows up in all the in-game cut-scenes which advance the plot. This can really add to the game's humor. If you make your character nude (and you really can make your character nude in this game) he/she will show up nude in scenes. Nudity in this game though has the breasts of females and the nether regions of both sexes intentionally censored through heavy pixelation though this adds to the humor of the game in a way.
+Good and highly dramatic, full-blown movie quality background music. Indeed, at times the background music was a wonderful parody of full-scale blockbuster Hollywood soundtracks (just as the plot itself is often a parody of full-blown Hollywood action movies).
+Pretty good, funny in-game radio stations throughout featuring lots of songs and even a little bit of fake talk radio. The game lets you choose your favorite songs from those included within the game and put only those on an additional "mix-tape" in-game radio station. I never really felt a need to import my own mp3 files into the game as a result.
+Lots of fun character and weapon upgrades throughout.
+While this game has a lot of standard Saints Row mini-missions, playing these missions is largely unnecessary and the main plot missions were the most fun and interesting missions of all.
+Not a frustrating game on casual difficulty. Easy in fact and yet still quite a lot of fun.
+/-While Saints Row 3 features a great deal of customization options, the detail of its options are not quite as technical or in-depth as its predecessor. Specific furnishings inside your different houses/bases cannot be customized at all and worse, one base of operations looks, on the inside, much like another, with almost identical floor plans and decor. You can customize what your gang members should look like but only based on pre-made templates.
+/-Good humor for the most part with lots of absurd and crazy situations which fit in well with a mostly interesting and extremely varied plot which does not take itself seriously. I did feel that the WWF parody wrestling boss battle was silly though. TV wrestling doesn't need a parody. It exists as a parody of itself. It is stupid and having a game make fun of how stupid it is simply makes that part of the game seem stupid in turn.
-Characters sometimes say repetitive and unhelpful things during missions.
-Saints Row 3 suffers from a more mild version of the same major problem which Just Cause 2 has. Saints Row 3 is full of interesting looking, well detailed locations but lacks enough interesting things to do in many of those locations. There are lots of mini-missions spread around but these missions, while varied, can get repetitive and still don't make fantastic use of the complex, urban environment which the game has to offer.
For example, there are lots of tall rooftops all over the city but very few missions will ever require you to get up on the roofs of many buildings. There are interesting industrial areas and shorelines all over the place but oftentimes they are merely there to be seen rather than interacted with. Buying properties doesn't let you interact with anything more than you otherwise could.
-Not enough DLC content ever came out for this game to give fans additional missions/stories to play through. Only 3 main story DLC's ever really came out and one of those is mostly just a succession of largely irritating minigames (Professor Genki's Super Ethical mini-mision garbage). Certain locations of the city seem a bit under-utilized by the time all the story content has been played through.
-The character creation options in Saints Row 3 are actually a bit less flexible and less precise than in Saints Row 2. Specifically, In Saints Row 3 there is no way to create a truly androgynous character. Sure, you can make a drag-queen character or play a female who speaks with a male's voice but you cannot create a female who has absolutely no breasts nor can you create male character who is incredibly skinny (indeed even the skinniest possible male character is still fairly muscle-bound). I would liken the degree of flexibility of Saints Row 3's character creation menus as being akin to those found in Skyrim.
By contrast, in Saints Row 2 I was able to create a character who was truly androgynous and quite thin. The new limitations to Saints Row 3's character creation system were irritating because I was hoping to use the same character I used in Saints Row 2 and I wasn't able to. In Saints Row 3 my male character was a muscle-bound grotesque by comparison and that quickly got irritating. I wanted a character who was impish and sort of thinly demonic looking and Saints Row 3 is simply incapable of making a male character like that. You can only make a really skinny female character. SEXUAL DOUBLE STANDARD ALERT though to its continued credit Saints Row 3 still allows you to make all sorts of fat looking people of either sex.
-Let's face it, your character is a mass-murdering psychopathic gangster ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ from hell. Even with massive character customization it's really hard to get involved or interested in a character like that or any plot he's involved in. In Saints Row 3 you play a villain. You cannot be a hero. You cannot even really be much of an anti-hero. It's hard to get involved with the plot as a result or to care much about any of the side characters no matter how nifty the plot is and no matter how many plot twists there are. In terms of plot and messages, there are a lot more meaningful and intellectually stimulating games out there. If the plot had been better, if it was possible to be some sort of true anti-hero, if the game had multiple endings depending on how well you behave or how evil you act in the gameworld then I would say this game was very good instead of merely 'good.'

The problem with classic card games on a PC is that they're easier to setup and play multiple times, which to me was one of the reasons to actually try to play every game, instead of just hitting Shuffle a few games until you saw one that you think you'd have a chance at.
FreeCell quest has restored that 'Must play Every Game' feeling!!!
Add to that an element of pressure (you'll get attacked), roll in a 'cheat' system, which we all did at one point playing the standard card version (spells), and an actual RPG/Character building aspect to put some fresh life into a classic for a whole new audience to enjoy.  This game will become your go to Windows game.
For those who have never played FreeCell, don't worry, this game actually starts out with a simplified deck to ease you into playing.  A choice of 'Classes' to fit your playstyle/skill level, or just to challenge is fantastic.
If you're new or a veteran FreeCell player, then you NEED to play this.  You will be hooked!

Rainbow Six Siege is an amazingly good fps game that implements a tactical element to it. The game is run by Ubisoft who are known to be an interesting development team, to say the least. There are quite a few bugs but Ubisoft does have a list of future ideas and is currently adding a lot of changes and patches to the game. However, with the release of operation Health, many fans are responding with controversial opinions due to the games list of current and active bugs that still haven't been fixed.
The Elo system has received a lot of controversy due to there being an array of bugs in both casual and ranked, the Elo system still works, however, it's not the best in the charts.
The system updates your current points to a level per win, this means if you are a bronze 3 and you win a game you will earn points, you will gain more points if you are more points you gain in the match.After every game, you will receive these points and they will add to your elo increasing it once you gain enough points you will rank up to the next level.
However the higher the rank you get the longer the wait time due to fewer people being in that rank, this is the main reason for controversy amongst the siege community.
Overall R6 is an amazing game however it does have a lot of apparent bugs with the elo and the gameplay.I love playing it and I am sure that you will love it too, there is a steep learning curve and a lot to learn with very interactive maps and each operator has a special feature and a counter.With Ubisoft supporting it for 10 years and aiming to have 50-100 operators I do think the game has a bright future however at the moment there are a lot of bugs but it is still playable and smooth.

Shovel Knight was a successful Kickstarter project developed by people who must really like the NES. The game is full with gameplay that was fun from that game system. There are elements being used from NES classics. The map is from Mario 3, Shovel Knight's attacks are from Ducktales and Zelda 2, the overall game design reminded me of Mega Man. The Xbox One version even has levels from Battletoads.
The numerous pitfalls I had (especially because of knockback from enemies) sure reminded me of the frustrating days of the NES, especially when destroying checkpoints. Shovel Knight is not a difficult game, but you can make it difficult depending on your playstyle. The feats/achievements of this game reflect this.
Gameplay of Shovel Knight is perfect. Both Shovel Knight and Plague Knight control really well and its fun to rush through levels because you get better at controlling them and knowing the layout of the level.
Yacht Club Games truely cares in developing Shovel Knight. Shovel Knight himself appears in other games and Nintendo even published an Amiibo figure. Currently the Kickstarter stretch goals are being made, where new gameplay mechanics are being introduced with King Knight and Specter Knight, just like they did with Plague Knight.
Shovel Knight found its way into my heart and made me feel the good old days being a kid playing the NES again.
